lessons.title: Records, costs, and selling the crop
lessons.titleSw: Kumbukumbu, gharama, na soko
lessons.briefing:
A farm without records is a hobby. Write seed, fertiliser, labour, water, and chemical costs. Weigh or count yields. Then you can say whether the enterprise made money.

Post-harvest: drying, storage pests, and clean bags. Aflatoxin in poorly dried maize is a health and market disaster. Grade produce; mixing rotten tomatoes with good ones loses the whole crate.

Marketing: know the buyer’s standard (size, pesticide PHI — pre-harvest interval). Selling before PHI is how consignments get rejected and people get poisoned.

Simple cash flow: money for harvest labour must exist before the broker pays. That is agribusiness, not “the rain will provide”.

options.text: How long to wait after spraying before harvest

exercises.explanation: Grade. Then pack.

options.text: Saves the rotten

exercises.explanation: Without records you cannot improve or access some finance.

options.text: Only WhatsApp jokes

options.text: Extra protein

lessons.title: Agrochemicals, PPE, and spraying
lessons.titleSw: Dawa, PPE, na kunyunyiza
lessons.briefing:
Pesticides are poisons with a label. Keep original labelled containers locked. A soda bottle of herbicide is how children die. Measure with dedicated equipment, not kitchen spoons that return to the canteen.

PPE: gloves, boots, overall, and the mask specified for the product — not a handkerchief. Mix in air, not in a store. Triple-rinse containers as taught; do not dump washings in a river.

Do not spray in wind toward people, water, or food. Buffer zones exist. Mixing two unlabelled leftovers is not IPM, it is gambling.

Re-entry intervals: the time before people can enter a sprayed field. Ignore that and you poison the weeding gang.
lessons.briefingSw: Weka dawa kwenye chombo asili chenye lebo. PPE. Usiweke dawa kwenye chupa ya soda. Usinyunyize upepo kuelekea shule. Fuata muda wa kurudi shambani.

lessons.title: Soil, water, and crop husbandry
lessons.titleSw: Udongo, maji, na mazao
lessons.briefing:
Know your soil. pH and texture decide whether fertiliser is used or wasted. Overdosing nitrogen burns and pollutes water. Follow a recommendation, not “more is greener”. Organic matter and drainage matter as much as a bag of DAP.

Crop rotation breaks pest cycles and balances nutrients. Planting the same family on the same plot every season trains pests. Spacing and seed rate are on the packet or the local recommendation — crowding makes weak stems and disease.

Water: irrigate to the root zone. Little-and-often on a baked crust can still stress plants. Mulch to reduce evaporation where taught.

Identify the crop stage. Spraying a flowering crop with the wrong product kills pollinators and can void a market standard.
lessons.briefingSw: Jua pH ya udongo. Mbolea nyingi si bora. Zungusha mazao. Fuata seed rate. Mwagilia kwenye mizizi. Usinyunyize dawa ovyo wakati wa maua.

lessons.title: Freshwater Pond Ecology, Water Chemistry & Fish Biology
lessons.titleSw: Ekolojia ya Mabwawa, Kemia ya Maji na Biolojia ya Samaki
lessons.briefing: Successful aquaculture is fundamentally water management rather than fish handling; if you care for the water, the water cares for the fish. In closed earthen or lined ponds, aquatic animals are trapped in their own metabolic excretions. Understanding the chemical equilibrium of dissolved oxygen (DO), un-ionized ammonia (NH3), nitrite toxicity, alkalinity buffering, and photosynthetic diurnal cycles is the line between a thriving commercial harvest and overnight mass mortality. This lesson establishes rigorous water testing protocols, pond engineering geometry, and biological profiles for the two pillars of tropical inland fisheries: Nile Tilapia (*Oreochromis niloticus*) and African Sharptooth Catfish (*Clarias gariepinus*).
lessons.outline: Freshwater pond ecology and primary productivity; diurnal cycles of photosynthesis and respiration (oxygen peak at 16:00, hypoxia crisis at 05:00); dissolved oxygen (DO) thresholds (minimum 5.0 mg/L for growth, emergency aeration below 3.0 mg/L); water temperature windows for Oreochromis niloticus (26-30°C) and Clarias gariepinus (25-30°C); pH scale (6.5 to 8.5) and total alkalinity as calcium carbonate buffering capacity; the nitrogen equilibrium in water: Total Ammonia Nitrogen (TAN), ionization fraction of lethal toxic free ammonia (NH3) versus non-toxic ammonium (NH4+) dictated by pH and temperature; nitrite (NO2-) toxicity, methemoglobinemia ('brown blood disease'), and chloride salt counter-measures; Secchi disk turbidity measurement and phytoplankton management (target 30-40 cm depth); earthen pond engineering: clay content testing (squeeze ball and ribbon tests, 20-35% clay), dyke slope ratios (2:1 interior, 1.5:1 exterior), pond bottom slope (1% toward drainage), monk sluice gates, and harvest sumps.

exercises.prompt: Why does the dissolved oxygen (DO) concentration in an un-aerated static fish pond consistently reach its most dangerously low levels between 04:00 AM and 06:00 AM just before sunrise?
exercises.explanation:
Phytoplankton produce vast oxygen during sunlight hours via photosynthesis. Once darkness falls, photosynthesis stops, but biological respiration by algae, fish, and benthic decomposers continues unabated, pulling dissolved oxygen down to its diurnal minimum right before dawn.

Why the other options are wrong: Cold water actually holds more dissolved gas than warm water; biological respiration is the cause of hypoxia. Ammonia does not directly consume dissolved oxygen through non-biological chemical neutralization. Evaporation is higher during hot daytime conditions and does not cause nocturnal hypoxia.

options.text: Cold night temperatures force water to expel dissolved gases into the atmosphere

Throughout the night, photosynthesis halts completely while both the fish and billions of phytoplankton continually consume dissolved oxygen via cellular respiration, depleting oxygen reserves until the morning sun reappears
Fish excrete more ammonia at night which chemically neutralizes all dissolved oxygen molecules
Pond water evaporates rapidly during nocturnal hours

exercises.prompt: In pond water, Total Ammonia Nitrogen (TAN) exists as harmless ionized ammonium (NH4+) and highly lethal un-ionized ammonia (NH3). When water pH rises above 8.5 and temperature increases, the proportion of toxic un-ionized NH3 increases dramatically; aquaculture safety standards require un-ionized NH3 to remain strictly below ___ mg/L.
exercises.explanation: Un-ionized ammonia (NH3) must remain below 0.05 mg/L (ppm). Above this threshold, gill epithelial hypertrophy, neurological damage, and mortality occur rapidly.

exercises.prompt: Match each water quality monitoring parameter to its critical diagnostic threshold or operational counter-measure.
exercises.explanation: Secchi 30-40 cm is ideal; nitrite causes methemoglobinemia treatable with chloride; Secchi < 20 cm warns of algal crash; DO < 3.0 mg/L halts feeding and growth.

right.text: Optimal phytoplankton bloom density balancing natural food and oxygen stability
Induces 'brown blood disease'; countered by adding agricultural salt (NaCl)
Excessive algal bloom with imminent risk of nocturnal oxygen crash or algal die-off
Sub-lethal stress zone; fish stop eating, requiring immediate emergency aeration

exercises.prompt: When excavating an earthen fish pond in clay-loam soil, what is the recommended slope ratio for the inside (wet) dyke walls, and why?
exercises.explanation:
A slope of 2:1 (2 m horizontal for every 1 m vertical) or 3:1 prevents dyke slumping. Vertical or 1:1 slopes quickly erode and collapse into the pond basin when saturated with water.

Why the other options are wrong: A 1:1 slope in unreinforced earth will quickly wash out and cave in under wave action. 5:1 is unnecessarily shallow, wasting vast amounts of agricultural land and shallowing water. Cardboard will dissolve instantly and timber will rot rapidly underwater.

options.text: 2:1 or 3:1 (horizontal to vertical), because steeper slopes will slump and collapse into the pond under wave action and saturated soil hydrostatic pressure
1:1 vertical cut to maximize the total water holding volume of the pond
5:1 slope on all sides to allow fish to swim onto the grass to forage
Vertical timber walls backed by untreated cardboard

exercises.prompt: African Sharptooth Catfish (Clarias gariepinus) can survive in stagnant, zero-dissolved-oxygen water and tolerate stocking densities above 50 kg/m³ because they possess a specialized arborescent accessory breathing organ known as the ___ organ, allowing them to inhale atmospheric air.
exercises.explanation: The suprabranchial organ (or arborescent organ) located above the gills functions like a primitive lung, enabling Clarias gariepinus to absorb oxygen directly from atmospheric air.

lessons.title: Hatchery Operations, Broodstock & Induced Spawning
lessons.titleSw: Uendeshaji wa Viatulio, Mifugo ya Mbegu na Upandishaji wa Kishawishi
lessons.briefing: Without a reliable, disease-free supply of vigorous fingerlings, an aquaculture operation collapses at the start. In the tropics, Nile Tilapia reproduce prolifically in grow-out ponds, causing severe overpopulation and stunted fish unless monosex all-male populations are produced. Conversely, the high-value African Catfish (*Clarias gariepinus*) will not spawn naturally in captivity, requiring artificial hormone induction (hypophysation), hand-stripping of gametes, and precision artificial incubation. This lesson details the science of sex differentiation, synthetic hormone dosage, egg stripping, water-hardening, and first-feeding nursery care.
lessons.outline: Broodstock selection and nutritional conditioning (minimum 35-40% crude protein feed); sexual dimorphism and visual sexing of Tilapia (papilla morphology) and Catfish (genital papilla shape and redness); the biology of Tilapia monosex all-male production: oral administration of 17α-methyltestosterone (MT) at 60 mg/kg feed to swim-up fry (under 11 mm) for 21 to 28 consecutive days; hormonal induction of African Catfish (*Clarias gariepinus*) using dried Carp Pituitary Gland (CPG) or synthetic GnRH analogues (Ovaprim / DHP at 0.5 mL/kg); intramuscular injection protocol; latency time calculation as a function of water temperature (degree-hours formula; 9-11 hours at 28°C); dry-method stripping of ova; milt collection and saline preservation; gamete activation with fresh water (60-second fertilization window); incubation systems (McDonald hatching jars, flow-through incubation troughs, kakaban mesh); yolk-sac fry absorption (48-72 hours) and first-feeding nutrition (Artemia nauplii, rotifers, and micronized egg-yolk emulsion).

exercises.prompt: Why is the 'Dry Method' strictly enforced when stripping and fertilizing African Catfish (Clarias gariepinus) eggs, prohibiting any water droplets in the collection basin until after milt is mixed?
exercises.explanation:
Catfish sperm and eggs are activated by freshwater. Once activated, spermatozoa exhaust their energy reserves in under 2 minutes, and the egg membrane swells and seals the micropyle within 60 to 90 seconds. If water enters before mixing, the gametes lose viability before fertilization can occur.

Why the other options are wrong: Catfish eggs are greenish-brown; color has nothing to do with marketability. Fish eggs do not dissolve in water; they water-harden and incubate in water. The dry method protects gamete fertilization mechanics, not fish temperature comfort.

options.text: Water dilutes the red color of the eggs, making them unmarketable
Catfish eggs dissolve instantly upon contacting liquid water
To prevent the female fish from feeling cold during handling
Water contact triggers immediate motility of spermatozoa and simultaneously initiates rapid water-hardening of the egg membrane, sealing the micropyle (fertilization pore) within 60 to 90 seconds

exercises.prompt: To produce monosex all-male Nile Tilapia populations and prevent in-pond overpopulation, swim-up fry under 11 mm in size must be fed a starter diet infused with the synthetic androgen 17α-methyltestosterone (MT) at a standard dosage of ___ mg per kilogram of feed for 21 to 28 consecutive days.
exercises.explanation: The globally recognized standard dosage for tilapia oral masculinization is 60 mg of 17α-methyltestosterone per kilogram of feed.

exercises.prompt: Match each hatchery breeding component or stage to its operational definition.
exercises.explanation: Kakabans support sticky eggs; MT masculinizes tilapia; latency dictates stripping timing; shooters must be graded out to prevent cannibalism.

right.text: Submerged synthetic screen where sticky catfish eggs are spread in a single layer
Androgenic steroid hormone used to masculinize sexually undifferentiated tilapia fry
Time elapsed between hormone injection and complete female egg ovulation (~10 hrs at 28°C)
Fast-growing fingerlings that must be graded out every 4 days to prevent sibling predation

exercises.prompt: What critical physical boundary dictates when 17α-methyltestosterone (MT) treatment must be initiated to successfully achieve 98%+ phenotypic male tilapia?
exercises.explanation:
Tilapia fry must be under 11 mm (swim-up stage, typically under 14 days post-hatch) for oral MT therapy. Once fry exceed 11 to 14 mm, gonadal differentiation has already started, making hormonal sex reversal ineffective.

Why the other options are wrong: At 50 grams, fish are already sexually mature and sex reversal is impossible. Broodstock are not fed MT; MT is fed exclusively to early post-larval fry. MT is administered orally in feed mash, never by micro-injection into eyes.

options.text: Fry must weigh at least 50 grams before hormones can be tolerated
Fry must be swim-up stage and less than 11 mm in total length, because gonadal differentiation begins after this size and later treatment fails to reverse ovaries
Hormone feeding is only administered to mature 1-year-old broodstock
Hormones must be injected directly into each individual fry's eye

exercises.prompt: At a standard tropical water temperature of 28°C, the calculated latency period for female Clarias gariepinus following an intramuscular injection of 0.5 mL/kg Ovaprim is approximately ___ hours before manual stripping of ripe eggs should take place.
exercises.explanation: At 28°C, the latency time for ovulation in Clarias gariepinus is approximately 9.5 to 10.5 (10) hours (calculated via ~280 degree-hours / 28°C).

lessons.title: Nutrition, Pearson Square Formulation & Feed Milling
lessons.titleSw: Lishe ya Samaki, Mfumo wa Pearson na Utengenezaji wa Chakula
lessons.briefing: Commercial fish feeds account for 60 to 70% of total aquaculture production costs. For smallholder and off-grid farmers, importing pelleted commercial feed at US\$700–900 per tonne is economically unsustainable. On-farm compounded feed, using locally available high-protein agricultural by-products, can cut feed costs by 40 to 60% without sacrificing growth performance. This lesson covers fish nutritional physiology, amino acid requirements, the Pearson Square balancing method for two-ingredient feed blending, Black Soldier Fly (BSF) larvae production as a self-replicating local protein source, and the mechanics of low-cost farm-scale feed milling and pellet drying.
lessons.outline: Fish nutritional physiology: amino acids as the primary energy source in carnivores and omnivores (unlike ruminants, fish preferentially oxidize protein for energy); crude protein (CP) requirements: fry 40–45%, grow-out Tilapia 25–30%, grow-out Catfish 35–40%; the concept of digestible protein and apparent digestibility coefficients (ADC); essential amino acids (lysine, methionine, threonine) and their primary dietary sources; key local feed ingredients: soybean meal (44–48% CP), fishmeal (60–72% CP, avoid un-dried locally produced meal), sunflower seedcake (34–38% CP), blood meal (80% CP, use at max 5% of diet), rice bran (12–14% CP, maximum 30% inclusion), maize grain (8–10% CP, energy carrier), BSF prepupae (Hermetia illucens: 40–44% CP DM, 30–36% crude fat); the Pearson Square method for balancing two-ingredient blends to a target protein level; farm-scale feed production steps: weighing, grinding to < 1 mm particle size, mixing, steam pelleting or ring-die extrusion, and solar-tray drying of finished pellets.

exercises.prompt: Using the Pearson Square method, a fish farmer wants to formulate a catfish grow-out feed reaching a target of 35% Crude Protein (CP), using Fishmeal (65% CP) and Rice Bran (13% CP). What is the correct ratio of Fishmeal to Rice Bran in the blend?
exercises.explanation:
Using the Pearson Square: Top-right (Fishmeal parts) = Target − Rice Bran = 35 − 13 = 22 parts. Bottom-right (Rice Bran parts) = Fishmeal − Target = 65 − 35 = 30 parts. Total = 52 parts. Fishmeal = 22/52 = 42.3%; Rice Bran = 30/52 = 57.7%. Verification: (0.423 × 65) + (0.577 × 13) = 27.5 + 7.5 = 35.0% CP. ✓

Why the other options are wrong: 50/50 equal blend would yield (0.5 × 65) + (0.5 × 13) = 32.5 + 6.5 = 39.0% CP, not 35%. This proportion gives approximately (0.35 × 65) + (0.65 × 13) = 22.75 + 8.45 = 31.2% CP. Fishmeal and rice bran are routinely combined in fish diets worldwide.

options.text: 22 parts Fishmeal : 30 parts Rice Bran (ratio 42% Fishmeal and 58% Rice Bran)
50% Fishmeal and 50% Rice Bran by equal weight
35 parts Fishmeal to 65 parts Rice Bran
Fishmeal and Rice Bran cannot be blended because their proteins are biologically incompatible

exercises.prompt: Black Soldier Fly (Hermetia illucens) prepupae harvested at the migration stage provide approximately ___ to 44% crude protein and 28 to 36% crude fat on a dry-matter basis, making them a self-replicating, zero-water-requirement local protein source perfectly suited for off-grid aquaculture feed supplementation.
exercises.explanation: Sun-dried BSF prepupae contain 40 to 44% crude protein and 28 to 36% crude fat on a dry-matter basis, comparable in protein quality to conventional fishmeal.

exercises.prompt: Match each feed ingredient to its most important inclusion limitation or practical risk in fish diets.
exercises.explanation: Blood meal limits palatability; rice bran goes rancid rapidly; groundnut cake requires aflatoxin control by heating; raw soybean contains anti-nutritional factors destroyed by heat.

right.text: Limits to 5% maximum inclusion; dark coloration and poor palatability reduce feed intake
High oil fraction rapidly oxidizes causing rancidity; maximum 20-25% inclusion
Must be heat-treated at 100°C for 15 minutes to destroy aflatoxin contamination risk
Contains trypsin inhibitors and lectins; must be heat-processed to destroy anti-nutritional factors

exercises.prompt: What simple standard field test should a fish farmer conduct to confirm that freshly produced on-farm feed pellets are of adequate quality before stocking them in the fish pond?
exercises.explanation:
Fish require 5 to 15 minutes to locate and consume pellets after broadcasting. Pellets that disintegrate within 2 to 5 minutes leach nutrients into the water, causing bacterial blooms, zero-growth of fish, and toxic ammonia spikes.

Why the other options are wrong: Aroma is not a reliable indicator of nutritional balance or pellet binding quality. Floating pellets are beneficial for many species (monitoring feed intake); sinking does not determine protein level. A quality pellet should resist crushing and hold shape. Shattering into powder indicates poor binding.

options.text: Smell the pellets; if they smell of fresh fish, they contain enough protein for good growth
Count the number of pellets that sink versus float; all good pellets must sink immediately
The 20-minute water stability submersion test — drop 5 pellets into pond water; passing pellets must remain at least 80% structurally intact after 20 minutes underwater
Crush a pellet between fingers; a quality pellet shatters into uniform powder

exercises.prompt: To prevent explosive mold growth (particularly Aspergillus spp.) and maintain safe feed quality during storage, farm-produced fish feed pellets must be solar-dried until their internal moisture content is below ___ percent, then stored sealed in cool, dark conditions for a maximum of 4 weeks for high-fat diets.
exercises.explanation: Fish feed moisture content must be below 12% during storage. Above this threshold, mold fungi proliferate rapidly within 48 to 72 hours, producing mycotoxins that suppress fish immune systems and cause mortalities.

lessons.title: Recirculating Aquaculture Systems (RAS) & Biofiltration
lessons.titleSw: Mifumo ya Mzunguko wa Maji (RAS) na Uchujaji wa Kibiolojia
lessons.briefing: Recirculating Aquaculture Systems (RAS) represent the highest-intensity, lowest-water-use fish production technology available. A well-designed RAS recycles 95–99% of its process water daily, achieving stocking densities of 50 to 150 kg/m³ — equivalent to a 1 m³ tank producing 100 kg of harvestable fish. The biological core of any RAS is the biofilter: a colonized surface area where autotrophic nitrifying bacteria perform the critical conversion of metabolically lethal ammonia into relatively harmless nitrate. Understanding the biochemistry of Nitrosomonas and Nitrobacter, the mechanics of solids removal, moving bed bioreactor (MBBR) design, oxygen supplementation, and carbon dioxide stripping is essential for designing, building, or operating a land-based RAS farm.
lessons.outline: The nitrogen cycle in RAS: fish metabolize dietary protein → excrete Total Ammonia Nitrogen (TAN) primarily through gill diffusion; Step 1 nitrification: Nitrosomonas europaea oxidizes NH3/NH4+ to nitrite (NO2-) consuming 3.43 g O2 per gram TAN; Step 2: Nitrobacter winogradskyi oxidizes NO2- to nitrate (NO3-) consuming 1.14 g O2 per gram NO2-; total oxygen consumption for complete nitrification = 4.57 g O2 / g TAN; hydraulic turnover rate: minimum 1 complete tank volume exchange per hour; solids removal as the first treatment step — swirl separators (passive radial flow separators achieving 60-80% TSS removal) and drum filters (80-95% removal); moving bed biofilm reactors (MBBR): high-density polyethylene (HDPE) K3 or Kaldnes media with 500 m² of protected surface area per m³ of media at 50-60% fill ratio; ammonia removal rate (ARE) 3.0 to 5.0 g TAN/m²/day depending on water temperature and DO; airlift pump design for combined aeration, circulation, and CO2 stripping; degassing column design; carbon dioxide accumulation (CO2 > 25 mg/L causes hypercapnia in fish); UV sterilization for pathogen control.

exercises.prompt: In a recirculating aquaculture system (RAS), why is it critical to remove solid fish feces and uneaten feed from the water before it enters the biological biofilter?
exercises.explanation:
Heterotrophic bacteria that colonize and digest organic solids reproduce every 20 minutes and have much higher oxygen demands than autotrophic nitrifiers (8-24 hour generation times). If solids reach the biofilter, heterotrophs establish dominance, suppress nitrification, and ammonia builds to toxic levels.

Why the other options are wrong: UV sterilizers are downstream of biofilters and solids removal; they do not address biological nitrification. Suspended solids do not contribute meaningfully to water temperature change. Feed intake avoidance is not the primary technical reason for removing solids before biofiltration.

options.text: Organic solids fuel explosive growth of fast-reproducing heterotrophic bacteria that consume most of the dissolved oxygen and outcompete the slow-growing nitrifying bacteria, causing the biofilter to crash and TAN to accumulate to lethal levels
Fish feces physically block the UV sterilizer lamp aperture
Solid particles raise the water temperature by thermal insulation
Fish actively avoid eating in the presence of visible floating feces

exercises.prompt: Complete nitrification of fish ammonia excretions in a biofilm biofilter requires two sequential bacterial groups: Nitrosomonas europaea converts ammonia (TAN) to nitrite, and Nitrobacter winogradskyi converts nitrite to nitrate. The combined total oxygen consumption of the complete two-step nitrification process is ___ grams of dissolved oxygen consumed per gram of Total Ammonia Nitrogen (TAN) processed.
exercises.explanation: Step 1 (NH4+ → NO2-) consumes 3.43 g O2 per gram TAN. Step 2 (NO2- → NO3-) consumes 1.14 g O2 per gram NO2-. Total: 3.43 + 1.14 = 4.57 g O2 per gram TAN nitrified.

exercises.prompt: Match each RAS component to its primary function in the recirculating water treatment train.
exercises.explanation: Swirl separator removes coarse solids; MBBR provides nitrification; airlift pump circulates while stripping CO2; UV sterilization destroys pathogens.

right.text: Passive gravitational radial-flow device removing 60-80% of suspended solid particles
Suspended HDPE media colonized by nitrifying bacteria converting TAN to harmless nitrate
Combines water circulation, oxygen dissolution, and CO2 stripping with no moving parts
Damages pathogen DNA to prevent bacterial and viral disease outbreaks in recirculated water

exercises.prompt: A freshly constructed RAS biofilter consistently fails to control ammonia even though Kaldnes K3 media has been installed at a 55% fill ratio and aeration appears adequate. The system was only started 5 days ago. What is the most probable root cause?
exercises.explanation:
Nitrifying bacteria are autotrophic specialist chemolithotrophs with doubling times of 8 to 24 hours — orders of magnitude slower than heterotrophs. A new biofilter needs 4 to 6 weeks of gradual, increasing ammonia load exposure to develop a full, stable biofilm capable of handling production-level TAN loads.

Why the other options are wrong: K3 media is designed to float freely in suspension — it must NOT be attached. Free movement is essential to biofilm stability. Chlorine is lethal to nitrifying bacteria and would prevent biofilm establishment. Nitrifiers grow across a wide range of TAN concentrations; the constraint is colonization time, not minimum substrate concentration.

options.text: The K3 media is incorrectly installed; it must be glued to the tank walls

The nitrifying bacteria (Nitrosomonas and Nitrobacter) have not had sufficient time to colonize and form a mature biofilm; RAS biofiltration requires 4 to 6 weeks of biological cycling before reaching full nitrification capacity
The biofilter needs to be disinfected with chlorine bleach before bacteria can colonize
Ammonia is too low in a new system; nitrifying bacteria only grow at TAN > 10 mg/L

exercises.prompt: In a recirculating aquaculture system, carbon dioxide produced by fish cellular respiration accumulates and causes hypercapnia. Fish begin experiencing clinical hypercapnia symptoms (lethargy, reduced growth, respiratory distress) when dissolved CO2 concentration exceeds ___ mg/L, making continuous CO2 stripping by airlift pumps or degassing columns mandatory.
exercises.explanation: Dissolved CO2 concentrations exceeding 25 mg/L in recirculated water cause hypercapnia: blood pH drops through respiratory acidosis, the Bohr Effect reduces hemoglobin-oxygen affinity, and fish exhibit lethargy, gasping, and suppressed growth.

lessons.title: Coupled Aquaponics & Closed-Loop Deep Water Culture
lessons.titleSw: Kilimo Mseto cha Samaki na Mimea (Aquaponics) na Njia ya DWC
lessons.briefing: Aquaponics represents the ultimate closed-loop food production system: fish and plants sustain each other in a coupled cycle where fish metabolic waste fertilizes plant roots, and plants biologically purify the water that returns clean to the fish. This eliminates the primary problem of standalone aquaculture — the costly, environmentally destructive discharge of nitrate-rich effluent. Simultaneously, plants receive a complete mineral nutrient solution with zero synthetic chemical fertilizer input. Well-designed aquaponic systems in tropical climates achieve fish yields of 40 to 60 kg per cubic metre per cycle alongside vegetable yields of 15 to 20 kg/m²/month. This final lesson covers media bed design with bell siphons, deep water culture (DWC) raft configuration, nutrient film technique (NFT), fish-to-plant ratio design rules, system cycling protocols, and the annual production economics of integrated aquaponic enterprises.
lessons.outline: The nitrogen cycle in aquaponics as the biological foundation: TAN → nitrite → nitrate via biofilm nitrification; plant roots assimilate nitrate (NO3-), ammonium (NH4+), phosphate (PO43-), potassium, calcium, magnesium, iron, and trace minerals; pH management (6.8 to 7.2 — the 'aquaponic sweet spot' balancing fish health and plant nutrient availability); plant production subsystems: (1) media beds — gravel or expanded clay (LECA) filled 30 cm deep, flood-and-drain using Affnan bell siphon auto-siphon; (2) Deep Water Culture (DWC) rafts: 25 mm polystyrene sheets floating on a 30 cm water channel, net pots holding plant root masses; (3) Nutrient Film Technique (NFT): thin film of nutrient solution flowing over bare roots in PVC half-pipes; fish-to-plant biomass ratio calculation (stocking 5-7 kg fish per m² of media bed as general rule of thumb); iron supplementation (chelated Fe-EDTA or iron filings in media bed); calcium and potassium deficiencies in fish-dominated systems; the Affnan bell siphon mechanics (standpipe height sets flood level, bell cap traps air, snorkel breaks siphon at drain level); PHOTO_CAPTURE practical assessment.

exercises.prompt: Why must the target pH in an integrated aquaponic system be maintained strictly in the range of 6.8 to 7.2 — a compromise narrower than the individual optima for fish, nitrifying bacteria, and plants separately?
exercises.explanation:
Fish tolerate 6.5 to 8.5; nitrifiers are optimal at 7.5 to 8.0 but function above 6.5; plants access iron and manganese best below 6.8. The sweet spot 6.8 to 7.2 is the compromise where all three system components remain functional without critically compromising any component.

Why the other options are wrong: pH management reduces stress but does not prevent all bacterial or parasitic fish diseases. Most aquaponic plants grow well at pH 5.5 to 7.5; fish typically need pH 6.0 to 8.5. At pH 6.8 to 7.2, NH3 fraction is actually very low, not maximized. Algae control is unrelated.

options.text: The 6.8 to 7.2 range is ideal because it prevents all types of fish disease

Below pH 6.8 nitrifying bacteria activity collapses sharply and iron and manganese precipitate out of solution; above pH 7.2 plant micronutrient availability is severely restricted and toxic un-ionized ammonia (NH3) fraction rises, so 6.8 to 7.2 is the only viable overlap zone for all three components simultaneously
Plants cannot grow below pH 8.0 and fish cannot survive below pH 9.0
The pH sweet spot of 6.8 to 7.2 ensures maximum TAN toxicity for algae control

exercises.prompt: In the Affnan bell siphon flood-and-drain media bed system, the siphon suction is automatically broken and the drain cycle is stopped when the water level falls below the open end of the small ___ tube, which admits atmospheric air into the siphon vacuum and terminates the drain cycle.
exercises.explanation: The snorkel tube (a small pipe penetrating the bell cap at a height 2-3 cm below the standpipe top) admits air into the siphon bell vacuum when water drops below its open end, breaking the siphon and stopping the drain automatically without any electrical timer.

exercises.prompt: Match each aquaponic plant nutrient deficiency to its characteristic visible symptom in growing plants.
exercises.explanation: Iron deficiency causes interveinal yellowing on young leaves; potassium causes leaf edge scorching; calcium causes blossom end rot; nitrogen deficiency causes uniform lower-leaf yellowing.

right.text: Interveinal chlorosis — yellow tissue between distinctly green veins on youngest leaves
Marginal leaf scorch — brown tip and edge necrosis spreading inward on older leaves
Blossom end rot on tomato fruits and distorted/blackened growing tips on lettuce
Uniform pale yellowing of all older lower leaves while young leaves remain green

exercises.prompt: Using the standard aquaponics fish-to-plant feed ratio rule, a farmer operating a 15 m² Deep Water Culture raft system should feed approximately how many grams of fish feed per day to maintain a balanced nitrogen budget?
exercises.explanation:
The design rule is 60 to 100 g of feed per m² of grow bed per day. For 15 m²: 15 × 60 = 900 g minimum; 15 × 100 = 1500 g maximum. At 4% feed rate (feed per day / fish biomass): 900/0.04 = 22.5 kg fish; 1500/0.04 = 37.5 kg fish — roughly 20 to 35 kg standing stock.

Why the other options are wrong: This dose is far too low — only 3 to 7 g/m²/day — creating severe nitrogen starvation in the plants. 200 to 333 g/m²/day would overwhelm the system, causing ammonia and nitrate accumulation. Plant nitrogen uptake is directly determined by fish feed input, which is the system's only external nutrient source.

options.text: 50 to 100 grams per day in total for the entire 15 m² raft
900 to 1500 grams per day (at 60 to 100 g of feed per m² of grow bed), supporting approximately 20 to 35 kg of fish biomass at a 4% daily feed rate
3000 to 5000 grams per day because larger raft systems require intensified feeding
Feed input is irrelevant; plants regulate nitrogen automatically regardless of fish stocking

exercises.prompt: Photograph your functional aquaponics system component, earthen pond, fish hatchery setup, on-farm feed production, or RAS biofilter installation from your aquaculture field practice. The image must clearly show: fish, plant production channels, grow media beds, bell siphon components, fingerling culture tanks, feed pellets, or water quality test equipment, with accompanying written notes recording measured water quality parameters (DO, pH, TAN, temperature) or system design dimensions.
exercises.explanation: Photographic documentation of aquaponic systems, fish ponds, or hatchery facilities verifies practical application of water chemistry, biofilter design, fish biology, and integrated plant production principles covered across this five-day curriculum unit.

rubric.criterion: Photograph clearly shows aquaponic grow beds, fish tanks, pond infrastructure, hatchery equipment, or feed production components with distinct legible detail
System components (bell siphons, net pots, aeration lines, biofilters, media, plumbing) or fish/plant subjects are clearly identifiable and in sharp focus
Written notes record at least three water quality readings (e.g., DO mg/L, pH, temperature, TAN) or documented system design measurements with units
Image is well-lit, properly oriented, and demonstrates safe handling practices and clean installation quality

lessons.title: Brakes, fluid, and diagnosis path
lessons.titleSw: Breki, fluid, na diagnosis
lessons.briefing:
Brake fluid is hygroscopic (it absorbs water) and it destroys paint. Wash spills immediately. Use the DOT spec on the cap. Do not mix DOT 5 silicone with DOT 3/4 systems. Bleed in the specified order until fluid is clean and firm.

Pads and discs: minimum thickness, even wear, no oil on friction material. A car that pulls left under braking is often one-sided: seized caliper, collapsed hose, contaminated pad — not “the engine is tired”.

Diagnosis path: complaint, evidence (test drive if safe), inspect, measure, cause, correction, retest. Parts cannon without evidence wastes the customer and fails assessments.

ABS faults need scan data. Unplugging ABS “to make it stop pulling” is not a repair.
lessons.briefingSw: Brake fluid inaharibu rangi na inanyonya maji. Fuata DOT. Pull upande mmoja: kagua caliper, hose, pad. Diagnosis: malalamiko, ushahidi, sababu, ukarabati, jaribio.

exercises.prompt: Brake fluid on paint should be:
exercises.explanation: Spill care plus the correct DOT type in the system.

options.text: Ignored; it improves gloss
Washed off immediately; it damages paint and is hygroscopic in the system
Mixed into engine oil
Used on the windscreen

exercises.prompt: A car pulls left when braking. Professional first path:
exercises.hint: Uneven braking is often one corner.
exercises.explanation: Evidence before parts.

options.text: Replace the engine
Inspect tyres, pads/discs, calipers, and hoses for a one-sided problem
Disconnect ABS permanently
Add oil to the radiator

exercises.prompt: Mixing DOT 5 (silicone) into a DOT 4 system is:
exercises.explanation: Incompatible fluids gel and fail.

options.text: Always fine
Wrong — incompatible fluids
Required annually
A type of bleed

exercises.prompt: After brake work you must:
exercises.explanation: Soft pedal is air or failure. Do not release the car.

options.text: Skip bleeding if you are late
Ensure a firm pedal and a safe test before handover
Disconnect a line for “feel”
Paint the discs

exercises.prompt: Brake fluid that absorbs water from the air is described as ___.
exercises.hint: Hydro-scopic in some papers; we use hygroscopic.
exercises.explanation: Water lowers boiling point and corrodes ABS units.

exercises.prompt: Pedal goes to the floor after a pad change. Trainee pumps it 40 times and wants to send the car. You:
exercises.explanation: A floor pedal is a danger. Stay on the job.

options.text: Send it — pumping is bleeding
Do not release: find the leak or bleed properly until the pedal is firm
Fit a wood block under the pedal
Disconnect a caliper to raise the pedal

lessons.title: Brake System Diagnosis: Hydraulic Circuit, Pad And Disc Inspection, Brake Fluid Change And Bleeding Procedure: Principles and Practical Application
lessons.titleSw: Brake System Diagnosis: Hydraulic Circuit, Pad And Disc Inspection, Brake Fluid Change And Bleeding Procedure: Kanuni na Utendaji wa Vitendo

exercises.explanation: Workplace health and safety regulations require pre-operational checks of all tools and PPE.

options.text: Begin operation immediately without inspection
Inspect PPE, workspace ventilation, and machine guards

exercises.prompt: Personal protective equipment (PPE) must always be worn to prevent ___ in the workshop.

exercises.prompt: Why is calibration and clean alignment critical in Brake System Diagnosis: Hydraulic Circuit, Pad and Disc Inspection, Brake Fluid Change and Bleeding Procedure?

options.text: To ensure precision, prevent joint defects, and guarantee durability
It is only required for cosmetic reasons

lessons.title: Week 4 — Cracked engine block: prove, classify, repair or replace
lessons.titleSw: Wiki 4 — Engine block iliyopasuka
lessons.briefing:
A cracked block is a diagnosis, not a guess made because coolant disappears. First rule out hoses, water pump, radiator, heater core, core plugs, head gasket, warped head, and porous gasket surfaces. Record the complaint: external leak, coolant in oil (“mayonnaise”), oil in coolant, white exhaust smoke, overheating, low compression, or combustion gas in the expansion tank. Never open a hot pressurised cooling system.

Clean and inspect. Cooling-system pressure test at the cap/manufacturer rating—not above it. Use UV dye if permitted. Combustion-leak/block-test fluid detects exhaust gas in coolant. Compression and leak-down help separate rings, valves, head gasket, head, and block. With the engine stripped, dye penetrant finds surface cracks on non-porous material; magnetic-particle inspection is for ferrous cast iron, not aluminium. A machine shop can pressure-test the bare casting and measure deck flatness.

Classify location and material. Cast-iron cracks in a non-critical water jacket may be repaired by cold metal stitching: drill stop holes as specified, install overlapping locks/pins, peen and seal, then pressure-test and machine if needed. Specialist hot welding of cast iron requires complete stripping, controlled preheat, compatible nickel filler, slow cooling, and post-machining; an unheated bead often creates a new crack beside the weld. Aluminium blocks may be TIG repaired only by a specialist after contamination is removed and distortion control planned. Cracks through main-bearing webs, cylinder bores beyond repair limit, multiple freeze fractures, or a badly distorted deck often make replacement or a remanufactured short block safer and cheaper.

Chemical “stop leak” is not a structural repair. It can block heater cores and radiator tubes. It may be an emergency measure only when the product/manufacturer permits and the customer understands the limitation. Final proof: pressure test cold and hot, check oil/coolant separation, verify compression, cooling-fan operation, torque records, and road test while monitoring temperature. Quote repair versus replacement with labour, machining, gaskets, fluids, warranty, and downtime.
lessons.briefingSw: Usikisie block imepasuka. Pressure-test mfumo, block test ya gesi, compression/leak-down, na inspect. Cast iron inaweza kushonwa kwa metal stitching au ku-weldiwa na specialist; aluminium TIG na specialist. Crack kwenye main-bearing web mara nyingi inahitaji replacement. Stop-leak si repair ya muundo.

exercises.prompt: Coolant disappears and oil turns milky. Before condemning the block, the technician should:
exercises.hint: Several faults mix oil and coolant.
exercises.explanation: A failed oil cooler, head gasket, cracked head, or block can produce similar symptoms. Evidence determines the repair.

options.text: Pour stop-leak and sell the car
Pressure-test, test combustion gas, inspect the head gasket/head/block, and document evidence
Weld the outside while the engine runs
Replace the radiator cap only and guarantee it

exercises.prompt: Why is a short cold weld bead on cast iron risky?
exercises.explanation: Specialist procedures use preheat/slow cooling or cold stitching to manage brittle cast iron.

options.text: Cast iron cannot melt
Uneven thermal expansion and rapid cooling can create hard zones and a new crack
Nickel filler is always plastic
Coolant makes every weld stronger

exercises.prompt: A crack through a main-bearing web should normally lead to:
exercises.explanation: The main web locates the crankshaft under high cyclic load. Casual welding can destroy alignment and safety.

options.text: Silicone on the outside
Engineering assessment and usually replacement/remanufactured block
A bigger radiator cap
Grinding the bearing shell thinner

exercises.prompt: The final acceptance test after a water-jacket repair includes:
exercises.hint: Prove the leak and overheating are gone.
exercises.explanation: A repair is incomplete until it holds pressure and the root cause of overheating is corrected.

options.text: Paint only
Pressure test, hot run, fluid-contamination check, temperature/fan check, and documented road test
One idle minute with no cap
Adding extra stop-leak

lessons.title: Week 5 — Radiator diagnosis, solder repair, plastic tanks, and flow
lessons.titleSw: Wiki 5 — Ukarabati wa radiator
lessons.briefing:
Start cold. Inspect cap seal, neck, tanks, seams, tube-to-header joints, drain plug, mounts, fan shroud, hoses, and staining. Pressure-test only to the specified cap pressure; too much pressure can create the leak you claim to diagnose. Remove the radiator if access or tank testing requires it. Plug openings and use a regulated water/air bench tester; never apply unregulated compressor pressure. Submerge testing uses low regulated pressure and bubbles to locate leaks.

Construction decides the repair. Older copper/brass radiators can often be de-soldered, cleaned to bright metal, fluxed, and soft-soldered at a tank seam or tube-to-header joint. Control heat so adjacent solder does not release. Damaged tubes may be professionally pinched and soldered only within an acceptable percentage; too many blocked tubes reduce cooling and require a re-core. Flush flux residue and pressure-test again.

Modern aluminium cores with crimped plastic tanks are different. A split plastic tank, hardened gasket, broken neck, or damaged crimp usually needs a replacement tank/gasket by a radiator specialist—or complete radiator replacement. Epoxy on a hot pressurised tank is usually temporary and may fail suddenly. Aluminium tube repair needs correct aluminium brazing/TIG equipment and skill; overheating thin tubes creates a larger hole. Bent fins may be straightened carefully, but punctured tubes and internal blockage need specialist evaluation.

Diagnose overheating beyond leaks: restricted core (temperature scan shows cold bands), external mud/insects, missing shroud, wrong fan direction, thermostat, pump impeller, air lock, head-gasket gas, wrong coolant mix, and weak cap. Final service: correct coolant type and ratio, bleed using manufacturer procedure, cabin heater hot, fan cycles, no bubbles/leaks, stable road-test temperature, and recovery bottle level rechecked after cool-down. Never release coolant to soil or drains.
lessons.briefingSw: Anza radiator ikiwa baridi. Pressure-test hadi rating ya cap tu. Copper/brass inaweza kusolderiwa baada ya kusafishwa; aluminium/plastic tank mara nyingi hubadilishwa au specialist. Epoxy ni temporary. Kagua flow, fan, thermostat, pump, air lock, na coolant sahihi.

lessons.title: Week 6 — Wheel rims: run-out, cracks, straightening limits, and safe rejection
lessons.titleSw: Wiki 6 — Rim: run-out, nyufa, na mipaka ya ukarabati
lessons.briefing:
A rim is a safety-critical rotating part. Begin with tyre condition and pressure, wheel-nut torque, hub face, bearing play, and impact history. Remove the tyre for a complete crack inspection when damage is suspected. Clean without grinding away evidence. Inspect bead seats, flanges, spokes, centre bore, stud holes, and the inner barrel—many alloy cracks hide on the inner lip. Dye penetrant may be used on clean non-porous alloy following its instructions. Magnetic particle is only for suitable ferrous steel.

Measure radial run-out (up/down) and lateral run-out (side-to-side) with a dial indicator on a clean mounted wheel; compare with vehicle/wheel limits. First eliminate tyre variation, rust between wheel and hub, dirt, and bearing play. Balancing cannot correct a bent rim; it only compensates mass imbalance. A wheel that needs excessive weights deserves inspection.

Steel rims with limited flange bends may be cold-straightened by trained personnel using controlled equipment, then checked for cracks, run-out, bead sealing, and coating damage. Do not heat a modern wheel with a torch: heat changes material properties and can start a crack. Alloy-wheel straightening/welding is specialist work. Cracks in spokes, hub/bolt area, multiple cracks, severe distortion, unknown previous welds, or manufacturer-prohibited repairs mean reject and replace. Even a repairable inner-lip crack needs alloy identification, controlled TIG procedure, machining, penetrant re-test, pressure/leak test, and run-out check by a qualified wheel repairer.

Never weld a rim with the tyre fitted or inflated. Heat plus trapped pressure can explode the assembly. Deflate, remove valve core, demount tyre, and clean flammable tyre products before any authorised hot work. Final fit: correct wheel size/offset/load rating, clean hub, hand-start nuts, star sequence, calibrated torque wrench, tyre pressure, and torque recheck policy. Document a rejected wheel so it is not put back into stock.
lessons.briefingSw: Rim ni sehemu ya usalama. Ondoa tyre ili kuona crack. Pima radial na lateral run-out kwa dial indicator. Balancing haisahihishi rim iliyopinda. Steel flange inaweza kunyooshwa na specialist; alloy crack inahitaji specialist. Crack kwenye spoke/hub mara nyingi reject. Usilehemu rim ikiwa tyre iko ndani.

lessons.title: Garage safety and lifting
lessons.titleSw: Usalama wa garage na kuinua
lessons.briefing:
A jack lifts; axle stands hold. Never work under a vehicle supported only by a trolley jack. Level ground, chock wheels, rated stands under specified points — not the oil pan, not rust. Gearbox in park/gear, parking brake as the procedure says (know when you must release it).

Batteries: acid, hydrogen when charging, and shorting a ring across terminals. Disconnect earth first on many negative-earth vehicles when the job needs isolation. Fuel vapour plus grinders is a fire. Spinning fans and belts take fingers.

PPE: boots, eye protection on grinders and springs. Coil springs store energy. Exhaust work on a running engine in a closed bay is carbon monoxide poisoning — extract.

Oil and brake fluid on the floor are slip hazards. Clean as you go. That is assessed.
lessons.briefingSw: Jack inainua; axle stands zinashikilia. Chock. Usifanye kazi chini ya jack peke yake. Battery ina asidi. Usifanye exhaust kwenye garage iliyofungwa bila extraction.

exercises.explanation: Stands hold. Jacks lift. Non-negotiable in NITA/CDACC workshops.

options.text: Leave it on a trolley jack only

Run the engine in gear
Remove the handbrake so it can roll

exercises.hint: Last off, first on is the positive on many procedures.
exercises.explanation: Follow the vehicle data. The principle is not to short the spanner to earth on the live terminal.

options.text: Positive first always
Earth/negative first to reduce short risk
Both at once with one spanner across

exercises.explanation: Use extract hoses. CO is colourless.

options.text: Better idle

exercises.explanation: Use the correct tool. Never improvise with rope.

options.text: Springs are light

lessons.title: Service to manufacturer data
lessons.titleSw: Servisi kulingana na data
lessons.briefing:
Service is not “black oil out, any oil in”. Use the manufacturer grade (viscosity and spec), the filter that fits, and torque on the drain plug and filter. Over-torque strips the sump. Under-torque weeps. Replace crush washers when specified.

Sequence: protect the vehicle, record mileage, inspect leaks and tyres, then fluids. Dispose of oil as hazardous waste. Air filters and plugs follow the schedule, not the customer’s cousin.

On modern vehicles, a service light and torque-to-yield bolts need data. If you do not have the book or a trusted information system, you do not invent a torque.

Road test or at least start and check the oil level again after the first run — filters fill and the level drops.

lessons.title: Flatting, polish, and handing back the job
lessons.titleSw: Flatting, polish, na kukabidhi kazi
lessons.briefing:
After cure, de-nib dust inclusions with fine grit, then polish as specified. Do not cut through edges — paint is thin on lines. Refit lights, mouldings, and tapes without scratching the new film.

Inspect in north light or a booth lamp: miss, dry spray, sinkage over filler, and unmatched colour (blend if the spec says). Clean the interior of dust. Torque bumper bolts to sense, not until they strip.

Customer handover: explain stone-chip care and curing time before a car-wash. Industry loses money on comebacks, not on an extra ten minutes of inspection.

lessons.title: Masking, primer, and spray-booth rules
lessons.titleSw: Masking, primer, na booth
lessons.briefing:
Isocyanate 2K paints need a specified respirator and booth practice. A dust mask is for dust, not vapour. Read the SDS. Mix by ratio, strain, and apply flash-off times. Mask adjacent panels properly; overspray on glass and rubber is extra labour.

Degrease before primer, and do not touch the keyed surface with bare oily hands. Build coats. Runs mean too much material or too close a gun.

Thinners are hazardous waste, not sink waste. Gun wash in the dedicated equipment. No smoking, no grinding next to wet paint.

lessons.title: Panel beating, cleanliness, and filler
lessons.titleSw: Panel beating, usafi, na filler
lessons.briefing:
Body repair is metalwork before chemistry. Knock and file to get the panel close. Filler is for skim, not to rebuild a wing in one lump. Degrease with the specified solvent, abrade (key) the surface, and apply filler in thin layers, allowing cure. Thick filler cracks and sinks.

Guide coat shows hollows when you sand. Work through grits as taught so scratches are finer than the next paint layer will hide. Bare metal needs the right primer — not random emulsion from the building store.

Dust from sanding is a lung hazard. Extraction, mask, and housekeeping beat sweeping clouds onto the next car.

lessons.title: Week 1 — Dignity, consent, safeguarding, and boundaries
lessons.titleSw: Wiki 1 — Heshima, ridhaa, na ulinzi
lessons.briefing:
Caregiving begins with the person, not the task list. Introduce yourself, explain each action, obtain consent, offer choices, and protect privacy during washing or dressing. Capacity can vary; follow the care plan and lawful representative process rather than assuming every older person cannot decide.

Professional boundaries protect both parties: do not borrow money, change a will, share photos, or accept control of mobile banking. Record gifts according to policy. Safeguarding signs include unexplained injury, fear, poor hygiene, missing medication, sudden financial change, or a caregiver who will not let the client speak.

Report concerns through the designated channel and preserve immediate safety. Confidentiality does not mean hiding abuse or a medical emergency. Write objective observations—what you saw and heard—not accusations.

lessons.title: Week 2 — Safe mobility, personal care, nutrition, and records
lessons.titleSw: Wiki 2 — Movement salama, usafi, na lishe
lessons.briefing:
Use the mobility plan and the correct aid. Check brakes on wheelchairs, clear the route, fit footwear, and ask the person to participate. Do not lift a dependent adult alone because you are in a hurry; use a hoist or second trained worker where required. Reposition immobile clients on the schedule and inspect pressure areas without massaging damaged skin.

Personal care uses clean-to-dirty technique and protects dignity. Food and fluids follow prescribed texture, allergies, diabetes, and swallowing plans. Coughing, wet voice, or choking while eating is a stop-and-escalate sign. Medication assistance follows the care plan; never crush tablets or change doses without authority.

The daily record states intake, output if required, skin changes, mobility, mood, and incidents. Never pre-sign a task. A falsified care record puts a vulnerable person at risk.

lessons.title: Hanging, ironmongery, and movement
lessons.titleSw: Kuning’iniza, ironmongery, na kupanuka
lessons.briefing:
Hanging a door: plane to clearance (often about 2–3 mm as taught — follow the spec), mark hinge gains from the hanging stile, chop or router to the leaf thickness so the hinge sits flush. Screws in the frame must bite — pack or longer screws into studs if the lining is hollow.

Locks: mortise at the right height, keep aligned, and do not split the stile. Handle sets have a backset. Test the latch before you call it done.

Moisture movement: a door hung in the rains on wet timber binds at the head the next week. Ease the high spot after checking hinges have not sunk. Advise sealing all faces, including the bottom edge, or the job comes back.

Ironmongery on exterior work should be the specified corrosion resistance. Bright mild screws on a coastal door rust and seize.
lessons.briefingSw: Weka hinge flush. Clearance kama spec. Fungua lock kwa urefu sahihi. Mbao yenye unyevu inasogea — seal pande zote. Test latch kabla ya kuondoka.

lessons.title: Workshop machines and joints
lessons.titleSw: Mashine za warsha na viungo
lessons.briefing:
Circular saws, bandsaws, and thicknessers remove fingers faster than any other college machine. Guards on, riving knife on, push sticks for short pieces, and never stand in the kickback line. Unplug to change blades. Dust extraction is health, not comfort.

Joints: housing, mortise and tenon, haunch, dovetail as taught. Dry fit. Shoulders must seat. Glue is not gap-filler for a 4 mm error. Cramp with protection blocks; check square as you tighten — frames rack.

Mark waste with hatching. Cut on the waste side of the line. A tenon that is too tight will split the mortise; too loose will fail when the glue dries.

Stop the machine fully before you clear offcuts. That sentence is in every accident report.
lessons.briefingSw: Guards na push sticks. Usisimame kwenye mstari wa kickback. Dry fit viungo. Gundi si filler. Zima mashine kabisa kabla ya kuondoa offcuts.

lessons.title: Measuring, face marks, and hand tools

lessons.briefing:
Joinery is accurate only if every cut is taken from known faces. Mark face side and face edge. Squares sit on those faces. A rod or cutting list beats measuring each piece from the last mistake.

Saws: a sharp saw is safer than a dull one. Support the waste so the last fibre does not splinter. Chisels: two hands, no body behind the point, knockers — not your palm on a stuck mortise in a hurry.

Moisture: wet timber moves after you hang a door. Store stickers, off the ground, as taught. Write the job size after checking the opening, not from the drawing alone if the site is out.

Assessors look at your marks. Faint, confused lines produce confused joints.
