lessons.title: Lime Chemistry & Calcination Kilns
lessons.titleSw: Kemia ya Chokaa na Tanuri za Kuchoma
lessons.briefing: Before the invention of Portland cement, civilization was built on the lime cycle. Calcium carbonate (limestone or seashells) thermal calcination yields quicklime (calcium oxide), a reactive chemical used in water purification, acid soil neutralization, sanitation disinfection, and hydraulic mortars that harden over centuries. This lesson covers the thermodynamics of the calcium cycle, limestone assaying, mixed-feed vertical shaft kiln construction, exothermic slaking, and pozzolanic hydraulic lime mortar formulations.
lessons.outline: The chemical lime cycle (CaCO3 -> CaO -> Ca(OH)2 -> CaCO3); calcination temperatures (850°C-1000°C) and enthalpy (+178 kJ/mol); limestone prospecting (acid effervescence test with 10% HCl or vinegar); vertical shaft mixed-feed kiln geometry (1:3 diameter-to-height ratio, tuyeres, refractory lining); slaking quicklime (highly exothermic reaction generating boiling heat and steam); safety PPE (chemical burn hazards from caustic CaO); hydraulic vs non-hydraulic lime; natural pozzolans (volcanic ash / pumice from the Rift Valley, pulverized clay brick dust).

exercises.prompt: A lime kiln operator allows the combustion zone to reach 1,250°C for several hours. When the discharged quicklime is later mixed with water, it fails to boil or slake properly. What happened chemically?
exercises.explanation:
Normal reactive quicklime is calcined at 900°C-1000°C, leaving a porous, high-surface-area sponge. Sintering above 1150°C fuses pores, reducing slaking reactivity from minutes to days or weeks.

Why the other options are wrong: CaO has a boiling point of 2,850°C and does not evaporate at 1,250°C. High temperature drives CO2 off; carbonation only occurs when temperatures drop below 500°C in the presence of CO2. Reducing CaO to calcium metal requires electrolysis or extreme reducing conditions (e.g., thermal vacuum with aluminium).

options.text: The calcium oxide evaporated into the exhaust gases
The lime became 'dead-burned' (over-burned); excessive temperature sintered the CaO crystal matrix into dense crystalline grains with minimal surface area, preventing water penetration
The limestone re-absorbed carbon dioxide at high temperature
The calcium turned into metallic calcium

exercises.prompt: The thermal decomposition of limestone begins around 825°C, requiring approximately ___ kJ/mol of endothermic heat, whereas slaking quicklime with water is violently ___, releasing 65.2 kJ/mol of heat.
exercises.explanation: Calcination is strongly endothermic (requires 178 kJ/mol heat input), while slaking is violently exothermic, boiling water and generating steam.

exercises.prompt: Match each stage of the lime cycle to its corresponding chemical compound and reaction.
exercises.explanation: The classic lime cycle: CaCO3 (stone) -> CaO (quicklime) -> Ca(OH)2 (slaked) -> CaCO3 (stone).

right.text: Calcium Carbonate (CaCO3)
Calcium Oxide (CaO)
Calcium Hydroxide (Ca(OH)2)
Recrystallized Calcium Carbonate (CaCO3) via air carbonation

exercises.prompt: Why will pure slaked lime mortar [Ca(OH)2 + sand] fail to set if used to line the submerged interior of an underwater cistern?
exercises.explanation:
Air lime hardens strictly through carbonation from contact with atmospheric CO2 gas. Underwater, it requires a pozzolan (reactive amorphous silica like volcanic ash) to create hydraulic C-S-H bonds.

Why the other options are wrong: Ca(OH)2 has low solubility (approx. 1.7 g/L at room temp), but it cannot carbonate without CO2. Quartz sand is inert and dimensionally stable in water. Freezing destroys uncured lime mortar completely.

options.text: Non-hydraulic lime requires atmospheric CO2 gas to carbonate into solid limestone; submerged underwater, dissolved CO2 is insufficient and the putty remains soft indefinitely
Water dissolves all calcium compounds completely within 24 hours
The sand expands underwater, breaking the mortar joints
Lime mortar must be frozen to trigger crystalline setting

exercises.prompt: To formulate ancient Roman hydraulic mortar that cures underwater, lime putty must be blended with a natural pozzolan rich in amorphous silica, such as finely ground volcanic ___ or pulverized red ___ dust.
exercises.explanation: Volcanic ash (pozzolana) or crushed baked brick (surkhi) contains amorphous silica and alumina that react with Ca(OH)2 to form water-insoluble calcium silicate hydrates.

lessons.title: Saponification — Soap & Glycerol Production
lessons.titleSw: Kutengeneza Sabuni na Glycerol (Saponification)
lessons.briefing: Soap is the foremost chemical weapon against infectious disease, physically dissolving the lipid bilayer envelopes of viruses and bacteria. When commercial supply chains collapse, soap can be manufactured entirely from two raw inputs: animal or vegetable triglycerides (tallow, coconut oil, palm oil) and strong alkaline lye extracted from hardwood ash (potassium hydroxide) or slaked lime treated with soda ash (sodium hydroxide). This lesson covers lye leaching, titration/specific gravity hydrometer verification, saponification stoichiometry, cold-process soap casting, and crude glycerol separation.
lessons.outline: Triglyceride ester hydrolysis equation (fat + 3 NaOH -> glycerol + 3 soap molecules); leaching potassium carbonate/hydroxide lye from hardwood ash (the floating egg density test); converting potassium lye to sodium hydroxide using slaked lime (causticization: K2CO3 + Ca(OH)2 -> 2 KOH + CaCO3); SAP (saponification) values of common oils (tallow, coconut, sunflower, palm); superfatting calculation (5%-8% excess oil for skin gentleness); cold-process method (trace identification, mould pouring, curing for 4-6 weeks); hot-process soap making and salt-out (graining) for pure soap curd and glycerol extraction.

exercises.prompt: A soap maker wants to make hard bar soap from pure coconut oil using a 6% superfat. For 500 grams of coconut oil (NaOH SAP value = 0.183), how much pure sodium hydroxide (NaOH) crystals should be weighed out?
exercises.explanation:
Baseline NaOH = 500 g × 0.183 = 91.5 g. With 6% superfat: 91.5 × (1 - 0.06) = 91.5 × 0.94 = 86.01 g.

Why the other options are wrong: 91.5 g represents 0% superfat (zero safety margin, leaving risk of harsh lye-heavy soap). This neglects the 500 g mass factor and simply doubles the SAP value. This would represent an excessive 18% superfat, leaving a soft and greasy bar.

options.text: 86.0 grams
91.5 grams
183.0 grams
75.2 grams

exercises.prompt: When dissolving sodium hydroxide or potassium hydroxide crystals, you must always add ___ into ___, never the reverse, because the violent exothermic dissolution can cause caustic liquid to flash boil and splatter into eyes.
exercises.explanation: Always add lye to water. Pouring water onto dry caustic causes immediate localized steam generation and explosive splattering of boiling alkali.

exercises.prompt: Match each soap-making term to its chemical and practical definition.
exercises.explanation: Trace marks stable emulsification before casting; superfatting ensures skin safety; salting out precipitates soap; curing cures and hardens the bar.

right.text: Point where oil and lye emulsion thickens so a drizzle leaves a raised mark
Formulating with 5-8% excess oil to ensure no harsh unreacted lye remains
Adding NaCl to precipitate floating soap curds and liberate aqueous glycerol
Air-drying cold-process bars to evaporate water and complete mild carbonation

exercises.prompt: In off-grid lye production, wood ash leachate produces primarily soft liquid soap. What chemical reagent is added to convert crude wood-ash potassium carbonate (K2CO3) into sodium hydroxide (NaOH) for hard bars?
exercises.explanation:
Causticization with Ca(OH)2 yields soluble KOH while precipitating CaCO3 chalk. Introducing NaCl salt brine to the boiling soap batch exchanges K+ for Na+ via the common-ion effect, precipitating hard sodium soap.

Why the other options are wrong: Acid destroys alkali, turning it into neutral potassium sulfate which cannot make soap. Charcoal filters colour and organics, but does not chemically convert potassium ions. Peroxide is a bleaching and oxidizing agent, not a cation-exchange or causticizing reagent.

options.text: Sulfuric acid to neutralize the potassium
Slaked lime [Ca(OH)2] to convert carbonate to caustic hydroxide, followed by common salt (NaCl) brine to exchange potassium ions for sodium ions
Charcoal dust to absorb the excess potassium
Hydrogen peroxide to oxidize the ash liquid

exercises.prompt: When testing the concentration of wood-ash lye with an uncooked egg, the egg should float with an exposed crown roughly the diameter of a ___ (approx. 20 mm), indicating a specific gravity of approximately ___ to 1.10 g/cm3.
exercises.explanation: An egg floats at a specific gravity of approx 1.08 g/cm3 when the solution contains about 10%-12% dissolved potassium salts, the optimal strength for saponification.

lessons.title: Ethanol Fermentation & Fractional Distillation
lessons.titleSw: Uchachushaji wa Pombe na Utengenezaji wa Dawa kwa Kunereka
lessons.briefing: High-purity ethanol (ethyl alcohol) is a strategic chemical asset in remote installations: at 70% concentration it serves as a broad-spectrum medical antiseptic; at 85%+ it fuels internal combustion engines; at 95% it functions as an industrial solvent and chemical feedstock. Producing ethanol requires two disciplines: biological anaerobic yeast fermentation of starches or sugars, followed by fractional thermal distillation to overcome the boiling point separation curves. This lesson covers saccharification enzymes, fermentation stoichiometry, pot stills vs packed reflux columns, foreshot/head/heart/tail cuts, and the 95.6% ethanol-water binary azeotrope.
lessons.outline: Biochemical fermentation equation (C6H12O6 -> 2 C2H5OH + 2 CO2); feedstocks (sugarcane molasses, cassava/sweet potato starch conversion using malted barley amylase enzymes); yeast vitality (Saccharomyces cerevisiae, pH 4.5-5.2, 28°C-32°C); distillation vapor-liquid equilibrium (ethanol bp 78.3°C vs water 100°C); fractional distillation column design (reflux ratio, copper packing, height equivalent to theoretical plate - HETP); cut fractions: foreshots (toxic methanol at 64.7°C), heads (acetaldehyde, ethyl acetate), hearts (pure ethanol 78°C-82°C), and tails (fusel oils); the 95.6% azeotrope barrier; safe alcohol hydrometer (proof) testing.

exercises.prompt: Why is it impossible to distill ethanol beyond 95.6% ABV using a tall fractional column operating at atmospheric pressure?
exercises.explanation:
At 95.6% by weight, ethanol and water boil together as a minimum-boiling azeotrope (78.15°C). Boiling does not change the vapor concentration; further dehydration requires molecular sieves or entrainer distillation.

Why the other options are wrong: Ethanol remains more volatile until the azeotropic point is reached. Copper is chemically stable in neutral alcohol vapors. Yeast remains inside the boiler and does not evaporate.

options.text: Water evaporates faster than ethanol above 90%
Ethanol and water form an azeotropic mixture at 95.6% where the vapor composition matches the boiling liquid composition, preventing further separation by distillation
The copper packing dissolves in high-strength alcohol
Yeast enzymes contaminate the column above 90%

exercises.prompt: During the distillation of a fermented wash, the first distillate to exit the condenser between 64°C and 70°C is called the ___, which contains toxic ___ (bp 64.7°C) and must be discarded.
exercises.explanation: The foreshots contain low-boiling volatile poisons including methanol, acetone, and esters. They must never be consumed or applied to open wounds.

exercises.prompt: Match each ethanol production term to its practical chemical role.
exercises.explanation: Copper scrubs sulfur; amylase unlocks starches; reflux multipliers column efficiency; 70% alcohol is the universal antiseptic standard.

right.text: Chemically binds and removes sulfur compounds and foul ethyl carbamates
Cleaves complex tuber/grain starches into fermentable simple maltose sugars
Condenses rising vapors to provide liquid reflux for continuous re-boiling
Optimal dilution for penetrating bacterial cells and coagulating vital proteins

exercises.prompt: When testing a tuber mash (cassava or sweet potato) after 60 minutes of mashing with malted grain, a drop of iodine tincture placed in the mash turns deep blue-black. What does this indicate?
exercises.explanation:
Iodine complexes with amylose starch chains to turn dark blue-black. A successful conversion yields maltose/glucose, which does not react with iodine (remains yellow/amber).

Why the other options are wrong: Alcohol does not turn iodine blue-black; alcohol fermentation only happens after yeast is added. Iodine tests for starch polysaccharides, not pH. Blue-black indicates unreacted starch, not sugar crystals.

options.text: The mash has turned into pure alcohol
The mash has acidified below pH 3.0
The enzymes were overheated and generated sugar crystals
Starch conversion is incomplete; complex starch chains are still present, requiring more enzymatic rest time or temperature adjustment before yeast pitching

exercises.prompt: For medical handrub formulation according to WHO guidelines, 833 mL of 96% ethanol is compounded with 42 mL of 3% ___ to destroy bacterial spores and 15 mL of ___ to act as a skin-protecting humectant.
exercises.explanation: Hydrogen peroxide destroys resilient bacterial endospores that survive in alcohol, while glycerol (glycerin) retains moisture to prevent nurse and patient skin cracking.

lessons.title: Biodiesel Transesterification from Seed Oils
lessons.titleSw: Kutengeneza Mafuta ya Dizeli (Biodiesel) Kutoka Mbegu
lessons.briefing: Diesel engines power essential heavy equipment: agricultural tractors, milling machinery, water well drilling rigs, and backup generators. While raw vegetable oil can run in a warm engine briefly, its high viscosity (10 times higher than petrodiesel) quickly leads to injector coking, piston ring sticking, and engine seizure. Through chemical transesterification, triglycerides are reacted with an alcohol in the presence of a strong base catalyst to strip the heavy glycerol backbone, producing Fatty Acid Methyl/Ethyl Esters (FAME/FAEE) with viscosity and cetane ratings matching commercial petrodiesel.
lessons.outline: Transesterification stoichiometry (1 triglyceride + 3 alcohol -> 3 fatty acid esters + 1 glycerol); alcohol options (methanol vs bio-ethanol); catalyst selection (anhydrous NaOH or KOH); free fatty acid (FFA) titration using 0.1% NaOH and phenolphthalein/turmeric indicator; the soap problem (moisture + FFA forms soap, preventing separation); batch processor design (sealed 200L oil drum, water heater element, 55°C temperature control, circulation pump); gravity settling and bottom glycerol draining; bubble washing and dry washing with wood ash; the 3/27 conversion test (fuel quality verification).

exercises.prompt: A batch of used cooking oil requires 3.2 mL of 0.1% NaOH during titration. Using pure NaOH crystals, how much total catalyst should be dissolved into methanol per 1 litre of this oil for complete transesterification?
exercises.explanation:
Standard base catalyst for dry virgin oil is 5.0 g NaOH per litre. The titration result (3.2 mL of 0.1% solution) directly indicates 3.2 g of extra NaOH needed to neutralize the free fatty acids: 5.0 + 3.2 = 8.2 g/L.

Why the other options are wrong: 3.2 g only neutralizes the free fatty acids; it leaves zero catalyst for the actual transesterification reaction. 5.0 g is the base amount for pure fresh oil with zero FFAs. In used oil, FFAs would consume part of this 5.0 g, causing reaction failure. This excessive amount would trigger severe saponification and lock the reactor into a solid gel.

options.text: 3.2 grams of NaOH
5.0 grams of NaOH
11.5 grams of NaOH
8.2 grams of NaOH (5.0 g base + 3.2 g titration extra)

exercises.prompt: During the batch transesterification of vegetable oil with methanol and KOH, the reactor temperature should be maintained at approximately ___ degrees C, because exceeding 64.7°C causes the alcohol to ___ and escape as vapor.
exercises.explanation: Reaction kinetics are fast and complete at 50°C-55°C. Methanol boils at 64.7°C, so staying below 60°C prevents boiling, overpressure, and toxic vapor loss.

exercises.prompt: Match each biodiesel processing stage to its underlying chemical mechanism.
exercises.explanation: Drying prevents soap; 3/27 tests conversion; glycerol is dense and drops out; water washing cleans the fuel.

right.text: Steam-flashes off trace moisture to prevent catalyst saponification
Verifies absence of unreacted triglycerides via solubility in alcohol
Dense crude glycerol mixed with spent alkali and soaps
Extracts polar impurities, free methanol, and micro-soaps into aqueous phase

exercises.prompt: What is the mechanical consequence of running an unmodified direct-injection diesel engine on unheated, raw, unrefined vegetable oil over several weeks?
exercises.explanation:
Raw oil viscosity is 10 times higher than diesel. Large droplets hit cylinder walls instead of burning in suspension, causing severe injector coking, blow-by, ring sticking, and crankcase oil polymerization.

Why the other options are wrong: Diesel engines require cetane, not octane; high viscosity causes thermal and mechanical fouling, not cool running. The governor controls pump speed; thick oil actually strains and can snap pump drive shafts. Emissions increase with unburned hydrocarbons, acrolein, and heavy black carbon smoke.

options.text: The engine runs too cool because vegetable oil has higher octane
High kinematic viscosity (40 cSt vs 3 cSt) prevents droplet atomization, causing unburned fuel to glaze cylinder walls, stick piston rings, and coke injector nozzles
The injection pump speeds up to dangerous RPM
The exhaust emissions turn into pure nitrogen gas

exercises.prompt: In the '3/27' fuel quality verification test, 3 mL of finished biodiesel is mixed into 27 mL of pure ___. If the solution remains completely transparent with no fallout, the fuel ___ the conversion test.
exercises.explanation: Pure biodiesel (FAME) is completely miscible in methanol at a 1:9 ratio. Unreacted mono-, di-, or triglycerides are insoluble and fall out as visible haze or oil droplets at the bottom.

lessons.title: Pyrolysis — Biochar, Pyroligneous Acid & Syngas
lessons.titleSw: Kuvunjika kwa Joto (Pyrolysis) — Mkaa Maalumu, Asidi ya Mbao na Gesi
lessons.briefing: Thermochemical biomass conversion (pyrolysis and gasification) extracts solid, liquid, and gaseous fuels from dry wood, crop stalks, and agricultural waste without consuming oxygen. In an indirect retort kiln, heating biomass to 400°C–650°C drives off three co-products: stable high-surface-area biochar for soil carbon sequestration; condensed pyroligneous acid (wood vinegar) for natural pesticide and antifungal foliar sprays; and non-condensable syngas (CO, H2, CH4) which can be flamed back under the retort to sustain the reaction autothermally.
lessons.outline: Thermal decomposition regimes (drying at 100°C-200°C, torrefaction at 200°C-300°C, exothermic primary pyrolysis at 300°C-500°C); mass balance split (30% biochar, 40% liquid bio-oil/wood vinegar, 30% non-condensable syngas); double-drum retort construction (55-gallon outer drum, 30-gallon inner feedstock chamber); condensing train (copper/iron tube in water trough) for raw pyroligneous acid collection; separation of wood tar from wood vinegar by settling; wood vinegar chemical composition (acetic acid, methanol, guaiacol, phenols) and agricultural dilution rates (1:500 foliar spray, 1:200 soil pest drench); syngas recirculation burner loops; PHOTO_CAPTURE assessment rubric of workshop chemical apparatus or test setup.

exercises.prompt: Why must raw pyroligneous acid (wood vinegar) freshly collected from a retort condenser be settled for 90 days before applying to agricultural crops?
exercises.explanation:
Raw wood vinegar contains suspended wood tars that coat and scorch plant stomata, stunting crops. Gravitational separation over 90 days cleanly partitions toxic heavy pitch at the bottom from the beneficial middle vinegar layer.

Why the other options are wrong: Wood vinegar is applied as a liquid foliar spray, not as a dry powder. Oxygen oxidizes alcohol to acid; it cannot turn acetic acid back into alcohol. Thermal pyrolysis involves purely chemical rearrangement, not nuclear reactions.

options.text: To allow the liquid to evaporate into a concentrated dry powder
To allow atmospheric oxygen to convert the acetic acid into alcohol
Because the liquid is radioactive immediately after pyrolysis
To allow heavy sedimentary wood tars containing toxic polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons to settle out by gravity, leaving clean, crop-safe wood vinegar in the middle layer

exercises.prompt: During the thermal breakdown of dry biomass inside an airtight retort, the reaction turns strongly ___ between 280°C and 450°C, releasing heat and combustible non-condensable ___ gas that can be routed back into the firebox.
exercises.explanation: Primary pyrolysis is exothermic; the breakdown of cellulose generates heat, and burning the returning syngas powers the retort without additional external firewood.

exercises.prompt: Match each biomass pyrolysis phase to its primary agricultural or energy product.
exercises.explanation: Zero waste: solid is biochar, liquid is wood vinegar, gas powers the kiln, bottom tar preserves structural timber.

right.text: Porous crystalline biochar for long-term soil carbon and CEC enhancement
Pyroligneous acid (wood vinegar) for pest deterrence and foliar health
Flammable syngas (CO, H2, CH4) for autothermal retort heating
Natural waterproofing and anti-termite sealant for timber fence posts

exercises.prompt: A farmer suspects their fresh biochar is under-cooked and poorly pyrolyzed. Which field test confirms the biochar contains harmful unreacted tars?
exercises.explanation:
Fully pyrolyzed biochar is dry, crystalline, and washes away as fine charcoal powder. Under-cooked biochar leaves greasy, sticky tar residue that smells strongly of creosote.

Why the other options are wrong: Fresh biochar can float or sink depending on pore wetting and moisture content; this is not a diagnostic test for tars. Pure carbon is non-magnetic unless contaminated with iron scrap. Elemental carbon is completely insoluble in mild acids.

options.text: The biochar sinks in water
The biochar attracts a magnet
Rubbing the biochar piece against the palm leaves a greasy, tarry, brownish-black smear that is difficult to wash off with plain water
The biochar dissolves completely in cold vinegar

exercises.prompt: Photograph a chemical apparatus setup, retort kiln, distillation condenser, or soap batch from your local chemical engineering fabrication practice. Ensure the image clearly demonstrates liquid separation, airtight sealing, or temperature monitoring, and include your written processing log.
exercises.explanation: Visual verification of condenser slope, airtight fittings, and phase separation ensures safety protocols and chemical yields are achieved in field conditions.

rubric.criterion: Photograph clearly shows reaction vessel, condenser cooling train, lye test, or finished chemical product
Safety precautions (ventilation, sealed joints, or protective equipment) are evident in the workshop setup
Written report records starting materials, reaction temperatures, settling durations, and output yields
Image is well-lit, in sharp focus, showing clean fluid boundaries or solid product texture

lessons.title: CPTED & Defensible Space Architecture
lessons.titleSw: Muundo wa Mazingira Yanayozuia Uhalifu (CPTED)
lessons.briefing: Physical security is not merely about steel gates and barbed wire; true security begins with landscape architecture and spatial planning. Crime Prevention Through Environmental Design (CPTED) uses natural surveillance, territorial reinforcement, and access control to deter intruders before they reach a compound. By structuring concentric rings of defense, eliminating blind corners, and enforcing clear sightlines, a small off-grid settlement can deter opportunists and coordinated attackers with minimal manpower.
lessons.outline: The four core pillars of CPTED (Natural Surveillance, Territorial Reinforcement, Natural Access Control, Maintenance/Management); concentric rings of defense (Zone 1: Far perimeter, Zone 2: Inner compound, Zone 3: Building shell, Zone 4: Hardened interior); sightline principles (the 2-metre/0.5-metre landscape rule); transition zones from public to semi-private to private; lighting geometry (glare avoidance, overlapping solar floodlights); eliminating concealment terrain and blind corners; community layout geometry (clustered homesteads vs isolated dwellings).

exercises.prompt: According to CPTED landscaping principles, how should perimeter vegetation and trees be pruned along security approach pathways?
exercises.explanation:
The 2-metre/0.5-metre rule eliminates concealment zones for crouching or standing humans while preserving canopy shade and low ground cover.

Why the other options are wrong: Dense high shrubs create ambush concealment right beside the pathway. Clearing 5 km is environmentally destructive and unnecessary; controlled pruning provides excellent visibility. Eye-level hedges blind defenders looking out from windows while providing cover for intruders.

options.text: Shrubs grown to 2.5 m height to block the view of the compound from outside
All trees cut down completely within 5 kilometres of the compound
Ground shrubs kept below 0.5 m (knee height) and tree canopies pruned up to 2.0 m above ground, maintaining a clear open sightline between 0.5 m and 2.0 m
Hedges kept exactly at eye level (1.5 m)

exercises.prompt: The four concentric rings of physical defense in depth, starting from the outermost boundary and moving inward, are: Zone 1 (Outer Buffer), Zone 2 (Inner Compound & Fence), Zone 3 (Building ___), and Zone 4 (The ___ Room).
exercises.explanation: Defense in depth moves from outer detection (Buffer) through delay (Compound Fence), barrier resistance (Building Shell), into the hardened last-resort Strongpoint (Safe Room).

exercises.prompt: Match each CPTED core pillar to its corresponding physical execution.
exercises.explanation: Surveillance provides visibility; territoriality shows ownership; access control channels movement; maintenance signals that the compound is actively defended.

right.text: Orienting primary living room windows toward livestock bomas and gates
Distinct stone curbs, clear boundary fences, and prominent perimeter signs
Thorny perimeter hedges channelling visitors onto a single gravel pathway
Immediate repair of damaged fence wire and clearing brush to show active custody

exercises.prompt: Why is it tactically counterproductive to mount unshielded, high-intensity floodlights directly above the front door of a defensive building?
exercises.explanation:
Light shining directly into the eyes of defenders ruins their night vision and creates visual glare. Tactical lighting should point outward from the perimeter into the clear buffer zone, keeping defenders in darkness while silhouetting intruders.

Why the other options are wrong: Modern LED floodlights use minimal power (10-30W); the problem is tactical optical glare. Insects are an annoyance, but the primary failure mode is tactical blindness of the occupants. Wall-mounted lights do not attract lightning any more than other metal fittings.

options.text: Floodlights consume too much diesel fuel
Insects attracted to the light will short-circuit the electrical panel
The bright glare blinds defenders looking out through windows into the dark yard, while casting deep protective shadows immediately adjacent to the building where intruders can hide
Floodlights attract lightning strikes

exercises.prompt: In defensible settlement geometry, grouping homesteads in a clustered circular boma layout is superior to scattered dwellings because dwellings provide mutual ___ of one another's perimeters and internal livestock can be protected inside a central common ___.
exercises.explanation: Clustered circular compounds eliminate isolated blind spots, provide overlapping fields of view, and protect vital assets (cattle, water cisterns) within an enclosed central courtyard.

lessons.title: Physical Perimeter Barriers, Fencing & Hedgerows
lessons.titleSw: Vizuizi vya Mzunguko, Wigo na Mipaka ya Miiba
lessons.briefing: No physical barrier is completely impassable; the primary objective of a perimeter fence is **delay**—buying critical time for defenders to detect, verify, and respond. A standard single-strand wire fence is breached in 10 seconds with hand pliers, whereas a properly constructed multi-strand high-tensile barbed fence backed by a ditch-and-berm or an impenetrable living thorny hedgerow (Euphorbia tirucalli, Sisal, Bougainvillea) delays intruders by 5 to 15 minutes while exhausting and injuring them. This lesson covers fence line clearance, corner bracing physics, concertina wire placement, anti-vehicle ditching, and biological thorny barriers.
lessons.outline: Perimeter boundary clearance rules (3-metre inside clear zone, 10-metre outside buffer); corner post anchoring and H-brace mechanics (box brace vs diagonal stay); high-tensile barbed wire stringing and tensioning (80-100 kg tension per strand); concertina razor wire deployment (pyramid configuration: 2 bottom coils, 1 top coil); ditch-and-berm anti-vehicle earthworks (1.5m deep V-ditch, steep inward bank); living defensive hedgerows: plant selection (Euphorbia tirucalli, Agave sisalana, Carrissa edulis, Dovyalis caffra / Kei Apple); pruning and interweaving techniques; gate construction and heavy drop-pin hinge security.

exercises.prompt: Why are the wooden corner assemblies of a high-tensile wire perimeter fence constructed using an 'H-brace' with a diagonal wire and horizontal stay, rather than relying on a single stout post?
exercises.explanation:
Multiple wire strands tensioned to 80-100 kg exert hundreds of kilograms of continuous inward pull. A single post will pivot through soil like a lever. The H-brace transfers this overturning moment into pure downward compression into the earth.

Why the other options are wrong: The purpose is purely mechanical tension support, not deception. Wood posts are non-conductive, but mechanical bracing is the sole engineering purpose. An H-brace requires two heavy posts and a stay; it uses more timber to achieve essential structural strength.

options.text: The H-brace looks like a gate so intruders mistake it for an entrance
It allows the fence to conduct electricity without grounding out
It saves timber by using smaller posts

The H-brace forms a rigid structural truss that converts the horizontal pulling force of tensioned wire strands into a vertical downward compressive force on the brace post, preventing the corner post from tilting or pulling out

exercises.prompt: To prevent unauthorized vehicles from ramming through an off-grid perimeter, an anti-vehicle earth ditch should be at least ___ metres wide and ___ metres deep, with all excavated material piled on the ___ side into an elevated berm.
exercises.explanation: A 2.0 m wide by 1.5 m deep ditch traps vehicle front axles, while the inner berm prevents rollover and provides defenders with an elevated rampart.

exercises.prompt: Match each defensive biological plant to its primary security property.
exercises.explanation: Euphorbia provides chemical irritation; Sisal punctures boots and flesh; Kei apple provides impenetrable thorn density; pleaching fuses living stems into a wall.

right.text: Caustic milky latex sap that burns skin and causes temporary blindness
Rigid fibrous sword-leaves ending in hardened 25 mm sharp puncture spines
Dense hedging shrub armed with rigid 50-70 mm needle-sharp woody thorns
Bending and interweaving young living branches to form a grafted solid thicket

exercises.prompt: What simple mechanical measure prevents intruders from using a timber pole to lever a heavy steel perimeter gate completely off its pintle hinges?
exercises.explanation:
If both pins point upward, a crowbar under the gate lifts it off in seconds. Inverting one pin locks the gate on its vertical axis so it can rotate freely but cannot be lifted off without unbolting or torch cutting.

Why the other options are wrong: Paint provides zero physical mechanical resistance. Grease smooths rotation, but makes it even easier to lift off. Wooden pegs are weak and easily sheared.

options.text: Painting the hinges red to indicate they are hardened steel
Inverting one of the hinge pins (e.g., top pin pointing downward and bottom pin pointing upward) or welding steel retention collars above the pins
Greasing the hinges with lithium grease every morning
Mounting the gate on wooden pegs instead of steel

exercises.prompt: In a 3-coil pyramid concertina wire obstacle, ___ coils are anchored side-by-side on the ground, while the third coil sits on ___ of them, forming an obstacle approximately 1.8 metres wide and ___ metres tall.
exercises.explanation: Two base coils anchored to the earth with a third coil stacked on top create a formidable triangular wire entrenchment that cannot be stepped over or easily bridged.

lessons.title: Watchtowers, Lines of Sight & Early Warning Sensors
lessons.titleSw: Minara ya Ulinzi, Nyanja za Kuona na Vihisi vya Tahadhari ya Mapema
lessons.briefing: A surprise attack at 03:00 hours against an unprepared settlement is almost always decisive. The defender's greatest tactical asset is **early warning**—detecting an approaching group at 200–500 metres rather than at the front door. This lesson covers the geometric siting and structural framing of timber watchtowers, line-of-sight dead space analysis, tripwire alarm mechanisms (mechanical pull-pins, 12V piezo sirens, blank 12-gauge perimeter poppers), acoustic gravel strips, passive infrared (PIR) battery relays, and the tactical integration of guardian animals (dogs, donkeys, geese).
lessons.outline: Watchtower elevation physics: Earth curvature and visual horizon formula (d = 3.57 * sqrt(h)); timber tower framing (4-leg battered pole tower, diagonal X-bracing, covered observation platform); dead space mapping (identifying dry riverbeds, gully micro-terrain shadows); non-lethal early warning tripwires (monofilament fishing line, spring-loaded clothespin switches, mechanical 12-gauge blank perimeter trip alarms); 12V battery-powered PIR driveway alert beams; acoustic crunch gravel paths (clean 20 mm crushed granite); bio-sensory security: domestic animals as early detection alarms (Guineafowl, Geese, Livestock Guarding Dogs - LGDs).

exercises.prompt: A watchtower sentry platform elevates an observer's eyes to 6.0 metres above surrounding flat terrain. Using the horizon formula d ≈ 3.57 × √h, what is the approximate line-of-sight distance to the natural horizon?
exercises.explanation:
d = 3.57 × √6.0 = 3.57 × 2.449 ≈ 8.74 km. Elevating the sentry to 6 m extends the line-of-sight horizon to nearly 9 kilometres.

Why the other options are wrong: 4.6 km is the horizon distance for a person standing at ground level (1.7 m eye height). 21.4 km would require a tower height of over 35 metres. This is far too low; even ground-level sightlines exceed 1.5 km on flat terrain.

options.text: Approximately 4.6 km
Approximately 21.4 km
Approximately 8.7 km
Approximately 1.5 km

exercises.prompt: When surveying a defensive perimeter from an elevated watchtower, hidden terrain features such as dry gullies or depressions that cannot be seen by the sentry are called ___ space, and must be covered by brush clearing or early warning ___.
exercises.explanation: Dead space represents blind spots where an enemy can approach unseen. These must be mapped and protected with secondary sensors or obstacles.

exercises.prompt: Match each perimeter detection technique to its operational mechanism.
exercises.explanation: Shotgun poppers give deafening location reports; clothespins make electrical tripwire triggers; gravel makes sneaking impossible; guineafowl provide living alarms.

right.text: 130 dB explosive acoustic report and muzzle flash indicating tripwire breach
Pulls non-conductive plastic tab to snap 12V contacts shut and trigger siren
Creates unavoidable loud crunching footsteps around building perimeters
Hysterical screeching flock alarm triggered by nighttime footstep vibrations

exercises.prompt: Why are the vertical support legs of a 4-pole wooden watchtower built with a 'battered' (inward-sloping 1:10) geometry rather than standing completely vertical?
exercises.explanation:
A battered tower forms a truncated pyramid. The broad base stance resists high wind shear and lateral sway far better than parallel vertical poles, preventing tower toppling.

Why the other options are wrong: Climbing outside poles is a severe safety hazard; towers use internal stairs or caged ladders. Poles used are straight, but set at an angle in the foundations. Rain shedding is the function of the roof, not the support legs.

options.text: To make it easier for sentries to climb the outside poles without a ladder
The wider base footprint significantly increases structural resistance to overturning moments caused by high wind loads and lateral seismic or dynamic movements
Because bent poles are cheaper to purchase than straight poles
To shed rain away from the center of the tower

exercises.prompt: To protect an elevated watchtower sentry from direct rifle fire, the perimeter parapet wall should be lined up to 1.1 metres height with double ___ or a 150 mm thick ballast layer of crushed ___.
exercises.explanation: Double sandbags or a 150 mm thick timber-retained crushed rock ballast barrier absorb and defeat high-velocity small arms ammunition, protecting the sentry.

lessons.title: Wildfire Defensible Space & Firebreak Engineering
lessons.titleSw: Nafasi ya Kuzuia Moto wa Nyika na Mistari ya Moto
lessons.briefing: In dry semi-arid scrublands and forested highlands, seasonal wildfires pose a destructive threat capable of wiping out an entire settlement in minutes. Over 90% of homes destroyed by wildfires are not burned by direct flame fronts; they are ignited by wind-borne blowing embers entering attics, eaves, and dry gutters hundreds of metres ahead of the fire. Protecting a community requires engineering three concentric defensible space fuel zones, plowing bare-mineral firebreaks, fitting 3 mm stainless steel ember mesh, and staging gravity roof-sprinkler systems.
lessons.outline: The Wildfire Triangle (fuel, oxygen, heat) and fire behavior factors (slope, wind, fuel moisture); the 3-Zone Defensible Space model: Zone 1 (0-1.5m Non-Combustible), Zone 2 (1.5-10m Clean & Green), Zone 3 (10-30m Fuel Reduction); firebreak width calculations based on flame length and wind speed; tractor disc plowing vs manual hoe trenches to bare mineral soil; wind-borne ember ignition physics and 3 mm non-combustible wire mesh screening for eaves/soffits; roof sprinkler systems fed by gravity tanks; fire-resistant landscaping plant selection (succulents, aloes, bananas).

exercises.prompt: Why are over 90% of homes destroyed in wildland fires ignited by blowing embers rather than by direct flame front contact?
exercises.explanation:
Wind-borne firebrands exploit small building vulnerabilities long before the main fire front arrives. Embers entering 6 mm attic vents ignite dry timber roof trusses from the inside, causing the structure to burn down while the surrounding yard appears untouched.

Why the other options are wrong: Wildfire flames reach over 1,000°C; the issue is that embers travel much further and faster than the creeping flame front. Embers are simply burning wood particles; their danger lies in wind transport and landing in unhardened crevices. Ember accumulation is aerodynamic, driven by wind and roof geometry, not magnetism.

options.text: Strong convection winds loft burning twigs and embers kilometres ahead of the fire, blowing them into unshielded attic eave vents, dry rain gutters, and debris under eaves where they kindle internal fires
Direct flames are too cold to ignite building timber
Embers contain chemical accelerants from forest trees
Because roofs are magnetically attracted to ash particles

exercises.prompt: In defensible space landscaping, Zone 1 extends from 0 to ___ metres from the building walls and must contain ___ combustible materials, utilizing crushed gravel, concrete, or bare earth.
exercises.explanation: Zone 1 (0 to 1.5 m) is the non-combustible apron. Any dry leaf, wooden planter, or mulch within this zone can ignite from falling embers and directly burn the wall.

exercises.prompt: Match each defensible space zone to its designated fuel management rule.
exercises.explanation: Zone 1 has zero fuel; Zone 2 manages canopy spacing and ladder fuels; Zone 3 reduces wild brush; steep slopes require double distance because heat rises.

right.text: Completely non-combustible gravel/masonry perimeter; zero mulch or firewood
Lean, clean & green; tree canopies separated by 3-5m and pruned up to 2m
Extended fuel reduction; dead scrub and brush cleared down to open woodland
Expanding Zone 3 out to 60m because fires advance twice as fast uphill

exercises.prompt: What mesh material and aperture size should be installed over building eave and soffit vents to prevent wind-borne wildfire embers from entering attic spaces?
exercises.explanation:
Plastic or nylon fly screens melt instantly when contacted by a 600°C ember, leaving an open hole. 3 mm stainless steel or bronze mesh blocks embers while maintaining necessary attic ventilation.

Why the other options are wrong: 15 mm mesh is far too coarse; small glowing embers blow directly through. Nylon melts and oil is highly flammable, worsening the hazard. Sealing vents entirely traps humidity, causing roof timber rot and mold during normal weather.

options.text: 3 mm (1/8-inch) stainless steel or bronze metal wire mesh (standard plastic insect screening melts under ember heat)
15 mm galvanized diamond chicken wire
Nylon mosquito netting coated in vegetable oil
Solid sheet metal with zero ventilation holes

exercises.prompt: To stop advancing ground fire, an engineered firebreak must be scraped down to bare ___ soil with zero organic turf, and its width should equal at least ___ times the expected flame length.
exercises.explanation: A firebreak must expose raw mineral subsoil (sand, clay, rock) with no dead roots. A width of 2.5 times the flame length prevents direct flame reach across the break.

lessons.title: Community Quick Reaction Protocols & Panic Rooms
lessons.titleSw: Mwitikio wa Haraka wa Jamii na Vyumba Salama vya Dharura
lessons.briefing: When physical barriers and perimeter sentries are overwhelmed by an armed breach, panic and disorganization are fatal. Surviving an attack or violent civil unrest demands pre-planned Community Quick Reaction Protocols (QRP), clear acoustic alarm signals, sector muster rosters, and structural hardening of an interior Panic Room (Safe Haven). This capstone lesson covers emergency alert sirens, internal door hardening, ballistic earth-filled walls, safe room life support supplies, redundant VHF emergency radio protocols, and field inspection rubrics.
lessons.outline: Community defense organizational structure (watch commander, quick-reaction patrol, medical responders, civilian shelter marshals); acoustic alarm codes (siren / horn blasts for fire, medical, perimeter breach); internal safe room hardening: outward-opening steel-reinforced doors, continuous heavy hinge pins, three-point deadbolts, ballistic sandbag/gravel wall retrofits; safe room life support (independent water supply, N95 smoke respirators, chemical toilet, trauma first aid, secondary battery power, VHF radio with concealed antenna); rehearsed evacuation drills; PHOTO_CAPTURE assessment rubric of a hardened entrance or perimeter.

exercises.prompt: Why should the reinforced security door of a hardened panic room / safe room always be mounted to swing OUTWARD into the hallway rather than inward into the room?
exercises.explanation:
Inward-opening doors rely entirely on the small strike plate screws, which shear off easily when kicked or hit with a sledgehammer. Outward-opening doors transfer all ramming energy into the massive structural rebate of the door frame, making dynamic entry nearly impossible.

Why the other options are wrong: While it does save space, the overriding engineering reason is ballistic and mechanical ramming resistance. The purpose is to keep attackers out, not assist their entry. Internal doors normally swing inward; safe room doors are deliberately reversed for physical security.

options.text: It saves floor space inside the safe room
To make it easier for attackers to enter if a fire occurs

An outward-opening door cannot be kicked in or rammed open from the outside; impact forces press the solid door leaf directly against the heavy masonry jamb rebate, transferring the shock into the walls
Building codes require all doors in a house to swing the same direction

exercises.prompt: To stop standard high-velocity small arms rifle fire (7.62 mm / 5.56 mm), internal panic room walls should be retrofitted with double sandbags or an interior wooden retaining frame filled with at least ___ mm of compacted dry sand or crushed rock ballast.
exercises.explanation: 150 mm (6 inches) of dense dry sand or crushed stone dissipates and captures high-velocity rifle bullets through friction and particle deformation, preventing penetration.

exercises.prompt: Match each community defense team role to its immediate tactical responsibility.
exercises.explanation: Organized defense requires division of labor: sentries detect, QRT fights/delays, marshals shelter civilians, medics treat injuries.

right.text: Rapidly arms, intercepts, and contains breaches to protect civilians
Directs elders and children into safe rooms and conducts headcount rosters
Detects incoming threats, sounds siren codes, and illuminates breach sectors
Manages trauma triage and shock stabilization within the safe room

exercises.prompt: Why must the emergency VHF/UHF radio antenna inside a safe room be secretly routed to a disguised or remote antenna outside?
exercises.explanation:
Thick concrete, steel door sheeting, and earth-filled walls heavily block RF electromagnetic signals. Without an external antenna feed, radio transmissions from inside the room will have a range of only a few metres.

Why the other options are wrong: The antenna transmits signals; it does not provide electrical power. Antennas do not explode; they simply suffer severe RF reflection and signal blockage. The purpose is two-way emergency communications on tactical frequencies.

options.text: To allow the radio to operate without a 12V battery
Because antennas inside small rooms explode when transmitting at 50W
To convert VHF signals directly into FM commercial radio
Dense masonry, sandbag walls, and sheet metal door cladding create a Faraday cage that attenuates radio signals; an external antenna ensures distress calls reach distant emergency channels

exercises.prompt: Photograph a physical perimeter gate, heavy door lock installation, watchtower structure, or safe room entryway from your community defense and workshop practice. Ensure the image clearly demonstrates hinge security, deadbolts, barrier anchoring, or clear sightlines, and include your written security audit report.
exercises.explanation: Photographic verification of physical security details confirms proper hinge pin inversion, deadbolt throw depth, frame reinforcement, and unobstructed defensive sightlines in accordance with CPTED and physical defense standards.

rubric.criterion: Photograph clearly shows reinforced gate, door deadbolts, hinge security, or watchtower observation structure
Structural fastening (3-inch frame screws, inverted pins, drop-bars, or anchor bolts) is clearly visible and inspected
Written report details defense zone assignment (Zone 1-4), potential attack vectors, and delay-time estimate
Image is well-lit, in sharp focus, showing clean structural fitment and hardware installation

lessons.title: Disease Transmission & the Epidemiological Triangle
lessons.titleSw: Uenezaji wa Magonjwa na Pembetatu ya Ugonjwa
lessons.briefing: Every disease outbreak follows predictable rules governed by the relationship between a pathogen, a susceptible host, and the environment. Understanding the epidemiological triangle, basic reproduction number (R0), herd immunity thresholds, and transmission routes is the foundation for all community disease prevention and outbreak control work.
lessons.outline: The epidemiological triangle (agent, host, environment); transmission routes (direct contact, droplet, airborne, faecal-oral, vector-borne, fomite); R0 and R_eff — what they mean for outbreak dynamics; herd immunity threshold formula; attack rate and case fatality rate; incubation period vs infectious period; the disease iceberg (symptomatic vs asymptomatic).

exercises.prompt: Measles has an R0 of approximately 15. A community of 1,000 children has 88% vaccination coverage. Is this sufficient to prevent an outbreak?
exercises.explanation:
HIT = 1 - (1/15) = 1 - 0.067 = 0.933 = 93.3%. At 88% coverage, 12% are susceptible — above the 6.7% threshold needed to sustain transmission. An outbreak is possible.

Why the other options are wrong: The 80% figure applies to diseases with R0 of 5-6. Measles R0 of 15 requires 93% coverage, not 80%. 50% corresponds to diseases with R0 = 2. For measles R0 = 15, even 90% coverage leaves enough susceptibles to sustain spread. Nutrition affects severity (CFR) but not whether measles spreads. Coverage against a threshold is the transmission control mechanism.

options.text: No — the herd immunity threshold for measles is 93%, so at 88% coverage an outbreak can still spread
Yes — 88% coverage is well above the 80% threshold for most diseases
Yes — once coverage exceeds 50% the outbreak will collapse
It depends on nutrition status, not vaccination coverage

exercises.prompt: The herd immunity threshold formula is HIT = 1 - (1 / R0). For cholera with R0 = 4, the HIT is ___%. For seasonal influenza with R0 = 1.3, the HIT is approximately ___%.
exercises.explanation: Cholera: HIT = 1 - (1/4) = 0.75 = 75%. Influenza: HIT = 1 - (1/1.3) = 1 - 0.769 = 0.231 = 23%. The low influenza HIT explains why annual flu campaigns with even moderate uptake can significantly reduce transmission.

exercises.prompt: Match each transmission route to its primary control intervention.
exercises.explanation: Matching the intervention to the route is the first step in outbreak control. Wrong interventions waste resources without breaking transmission.

right.text: Negative-pressure isolation rooms and N95 respirators
Safe water, sanitation, and handwashing (WASH)
Insecticide-treated bed nets and indoor residual spraying
Surgical masks, 1 m physical distancing

exercises.prompt: During a cholera outbreak, 3,200 people drank water from a contaminated river. 480 developed cholera. 12 of those died. What are the attack rate and case fatality rate?
exercises.explanation:
AR = 480/3200 x 100 = 15%. CFR = 12/480 x 100 = 2.5%. A CFR of 2.5% indicates some access to ORT treatment (untreated cholera CFR is 25-50%).

Why the other options are wrong: These are reversed. AR uses the exposed population (3,200) as denominator; CFR uses confirmed cases (480) as denominator. AR is correct. CFR is not deaths/exposed but deaths/confirmed cases: 12/480 = 2.5%, not 0.37%. 0.37% would be deaths/exposed (12/3200). AR is cases/exposed = 480/3200 = 15%.

exercises.prompt: For every 1 paralytic polio case seen, approximately ___ people are actually infected (the disease iceberg). During a COVID-19 wave where 30% of infections are symptomatic, if a clinic records 600 symptomatic cases, the estimated true infection count is ___.
exercises.explanation: Polio: 1 paralytic per 200 infected = iceberg ratio of 200. COVID-19: 600 symptomatic = 30% of total; total = 600/0.30 = 2,000 true infections. This undercounting has major implications for surveillance — reported cases are always a fraction of true burden.

lessons.title: Oral Rehydration Therapy & Diarrhoeal Disease
lessons.titleSw: Tiba ya Maji kwa Mdomo na Magonjwa ya Kuhara
lessons.briefing: Diarrhoeal disease kills approximately 1.6 million people per year globally — the vast majority are children under 5 in low-income settings. Oral rehydration therapy (ORT), a simple solution of sugar, salt, and water, can reduce cholera CFR from 50% to under 1%. Every community health worker must be able to prepare ORT from local materials, assess dehydration severity, and know when to escalate to intravenous fluids.
lessons.outline: Pathophysiology of secretory diarrhoea; WHO dehydration assessment (no dehydration, some dehydration, severe dehydration); WHO ORS formulation and home-made alternatives; ORT administration rates (Plan A, B, C); zinc supplementation evidence; BRAT/BRAF diet guidance; danger signs requiring IV fluids or hospital referral; cholera cot setup for mass casualty events.

exercises.prompt: A 15 kg child has sunken eyes, is drinking eagerly, and skin pinch returns in 1.5 seconds. What WHO dehydration classification and treatment plan apply?
exercises.explanation:
Sunken eyes + thirsty (drinks eagerly) = 2 signs of 'some dehydration'. Plan B: 75 mL/kg x 15 kg = 1,125 mL over 4 hours = approximately 281 mL/hour. Re-assess after 4 hours.

Why the other options are wrong: Severe dehydration requires lethargic/unconscious + very sunken eyes + very slow (>2s) skin pinch. At 1.5s skin pinch and drinking eagerly, this is 'some' not 'severe' dehydration. Two clinical signs (sunken eyes, thirsty) confirm 'some dehydration' — Plan A is insufficient. Plan B ORS rehydration over 4 hours is needed. Plan B is 75 mL/kg over 4 hours. The 100 mL/kg over 6 hours is the IV regimen for Plan C in children under 5.

options.text: Some dehydration — Plan B: 75 mL/kg ORS over 4 hours = 1,125 mL
Severe dehydration — Plan C: IV Ringer's Lactate 100 mL/kg
No dehydration — Plan A: ORS after every loose stool only
Some dehydration — Plan B: 100 mL/kg over 6 hours

exercises.prompt: Home-made ORT uses 1 litre of clean water with ___ teaspoons of sugar and ___ teaspoon of salt. WHO recommends zinc supplementation for children under 5 for ___ days alongside ORT.
exercises.explanation: Home ORT: 6 level teaspoons sugar (30 g) + 0.5 teaspoon salt (2.5 g) per litre. Home ORT lacks potassium and bicarbonate found in WHO ORS sachets — it is a temporary measure only. Zinc: 10-14 days reduces episode duration by 25% and prevents future episodes for 2-3 months.

exercises.prompt: Match each dehydration sign to its severity category.
exercises.explanation: The WHO skin pinch test is key: immediate return = no dehydration; slow (<2s) = some; very slow (>2s) = severe. Two or more signs in a severity category are required for that classification.

left.text: Skin pinch returns in 3 seconds, patient unconscious

right.text: Severe dehydration

left.text: Child restless and irritable, eyes sunken, drinking eagerly

right.text: Some dehydration

left.text: Child well and alert, eyes normal, moist tongue

right.text: No dehydration

left.text: Very dry mouth, unable to drink, very sunken eyes

right.text: Severe dehydration

exercises.prompt: Why does oral rehydration therapy work even when the cholera toxin is causing massive fluid secretion in the gut?
exercises.explanation:
Cholera toxin activates adenylate cyclase (cAMP), forcing Cl- secretion. However, the SGLT1 absorptive pathway is a completely separate mechanism — glucose carries Na+ across the enterocyte even during maximal secretion. ORT exploits this parallel absorption pathway.

Why the other options are wrong: There is no antitoxin in ORS. ORS does not neutralise cholera toxin. It works around the toxin by using a different absorptive pathway. ORS salt concentrations are far too low to be antibacterial. ORS replaces lost fluids and electrolytes — it does not treat the infection. ORS does not induce vomiting. It is given orally in small sips specifically to prevent vomiting. Vomiting is a danger sign requiring reassessment.

options.text: ORS neutralises the cholera toxin directly, stopping the secretory diarrhoea
Salt in ORS kills the Vibrio cholerae bacteria in the gut
Glucose activates the SGLT1 sodium-glucose co-transporter, which remains functional even when the secretory cAMP pump is active, allowing net sodium and water absorption
ORS induces vomiting of the toxin before it can cause secretion

exercises.prompt: Untreated cholera has a case fatality rate of ___%, which drops to below ___% with prompt oral rehydration therapy. A 25 kg child classified as Plan B needs ___ mL of ORS over 4 hours.
exercises.explanation: Untreated cholera CFR is 25-50% from dehydration alone. With ORT CFR drops below 1% — one of the most dramatic treatment effects in all of medicine. Plan B: 75 mL/kg x 25 kg = 1,875 mL over 4 hours.

lessons.title: Malaria — Lifecycle, Diagnosis & ACT Treatment
lessons.titleSw: Malaria — Mzunguko wa Maisha, Utambuzi na Matibabu ya ACT
lessons.briefing: Malaria causes over 600,000 deaths per year, over 95% in sub-Saharan Africa, and over 80% in children under 5. Kenya has high malaria burden in lakeside, coastal, and western regions. A community health worker equipped with a rapid diagnostic test (RDT) and artemisinin-based combination therapy (ACT) can test, diagnose, and treat uncomplicated malaria at the household level — saving lives before referral is possible.
lessons.outline: Plasmodium species (falciparum, vivax, malariae, ovale); Anopheles mosquito lifecycle and biting behaviour; clinical presentation (uncomplicated vs severe malaria); rapid diagnostic tests (RDT) — HRP2 antigen basis, procedure, and reading results; artemisinin-based combination therapy (ACT) dosing by weight; artemether-lumefantrine (AL) 6-dose regimen; danger signs requiring referral; insecticide-treated bed nets (ITNs) and indoor residual spraying (IRS).

exercises.prompt: A 7-year-old child (22 kg) has a positive RDT and fever. What is the correct AL dosing regimen for this child?
exercises.explanation:
22 kg falls in the 15-24 kg weight band = 2 tablets per dose. The 6-dose regimen spans 3 days: 0h, 8h, then twice daily (24h, 36h, 48h, 60h). Fatty food increases AL absorption 3-fold.

Why the other options are wrong: 1 tablet is the dose for children 5-14 kg. At 22 kg the dose is 2 tablets per dose. 4 tablets is for adults 35 kg and above. Paediatric dosing is weight-banded. 22 kg = 2 tablets per dose, not a single adult dose. AL is a 6-dose 3-day regimen (not 5 days, not twice daily for the full period — doses are at 0h, 8h, 24h, 36h, 48h, 60h).

options.text: 2 tablets at 0h, 8h, 24h, 36h, 48h and 60h — give with food such as peanuts or milk
1 tablet at 0h, 8h, 24h, 36h, 48h and 60h
4 tablets in a single dose — adults and children over 15 kg take the same dose
2 tablets twice daily for 5 days

exercises.prompt: Female Anopheles mosquitoes peak biting time is between ___h and ___h. The incubation period for P. falciparum in the human after a bite is ___ to ___ days.
exercises.explanation: Peak biting 2200h-0200h is why sleeping under an ITN during these hours is the primary protection. Incubation of 7-14 days means a returning traveller may not be symptomatic until 2 weeks after the infective bite — important for clinical history taking.

exercises.prompt: Match each severe malaria danger sign to its physiological cause.
exercises.explanation: P. falciparum causes severe disease through multiple mechanisms acting simultaneously. Each danger sign reflects a different organ system failure and is an independent indication for urgent IV artesunate + referral.

right.text: Cerebral malaria — parasitised RBCs sequestered in brain capillaries
Blackwater fever — massive haemolysis releasing haemoglobin in urine
Destruction of red blood cells by parasite replication cycles
Parasite glucose consumption + impaired hepatic gluconeogenesis

exercises.prompt: An RDT shows no line in the Control (C) position after 20 minutes. What should the community health worker do?
exercises.explanation:
The control line must always appear — its presence confirms the test ran correctly. No C line = invalid test regardless of T line status. Repeat with a new kit from a different lot if repeated invalids occur (possible storage problem).

Why the other options are wrong: No C line does not mean negative. It means the test failed. A valid negative shows C line only. Without C line the test gives no diagnostic information. A positive result shows C + T lines. No C line means invalid, regardless of whether T appears. The test has not functioned correctly. Kenya NMCP guidelines: treat only confirmed positives. Give empirical ACT only in high-transmission areas when RDT is unavailable. Repeat the test first.

options.text: The patient is negative for malaria — treat the fever as another cause
The patient is strongly positive — two lines always indicate severe infection
Give ACT immediately as a precaution since the result is unclear
The test is invalid — discard it and repeat with a new RDT kit

exercises.prompt: Long-lasting insecticidal nets (LLINs) retain efficacy for approximately ___ years and reduce child malaria mortality by approximately ___%. A patient who vomits AL within ___ minutes of a dose should receive the same dose again.
exercises.explanation: LLINs: factory-impregnated to last 3 years even with washing. 50% mortality reduction (RCT evidence, WHO malaria report 2023). AL vomiting: if < 30 minutes since ingestion, repeat the same dose (the tablet has not been absorbed). If > 30 minutes, do not repeat (assume absorbed even if some vomiting occurs).

lessons.title: Vaccination Cold Chain & Immunisation Logistics
lessons.titleSw: Mnyororo Baridi wa Chanjo na Usimamizi wa Kinga
lessons.briefing: Vaccines are among the most cost-effective health interventions ever developed, but they are utterly dependent on a functioning cold chain. In East Africa's last-mile settings, a single power outage or broken refrigerator door seal can destroy an entire vaccine stock. Community health workers and vaccinators must master temperature monitoring, vaccine vial monitor (VVM) interpretation, and cold-box packing to protect every dose.
lessons.outline: Kenya Expanded Programme on Immunisation (KEPI) schedule and antigens; cold chain temperature requirements (+2 to +8 degrees C, no freezing for most); freeze-sensitive vaccines (HepB, liquid pentavalent, HPV); vaccine vial monitor (VVM) stages and discard rules; cold box and vaccine carrier packing; temperature monitoring (Fridge-tag, manual log); open vial policy by antigen; vaccine wastage calculation and target rates.

exercises.prompt: A health worker checks a Pentavalent vial and finds the inner VVM square is darker than the outer ring. The expiry date is still 3 months away. What should be done?
exercises.explanation:
VVM Stage 3 (inner darker than outer) = discard immediately. VVM indicates accumulated heat exposure that has likely compromised potency — expiry date only measures time, not heat. Both conditions must be met: VVM Stage 1-2 AND within expiry date.

Why the other options are wrong: Expiry date and VVM are independent checks. A VVM Stage 3 or 4 overrides a valid expiry date. The vaccine may have been heat-exposed and is potentially non-immunogenic. The shake test checks for freeze damage in freeze-sensitive vaccines. VVM Stage 3 indicates heat damage — a completely different issue. The answer is clear: discard. VVM Stage 3 is a discard instruction, not a prioritisation signal. Stage 2 (same colour) triggers prioritisation. Stage 3 (darker) = discard regardless.

options.text: Use the vial — the expiry date is still valid for 3 more months
Shake the vial to check for freeze damage before deciding
Discard the vial and report — VVM Stage 3/4 means heat damage regardless of expiry date
Use the vial first and prioritise it before newer stock

exercises.prompt: Cold chain vaccines must be stored at ___ to ___ degrees C. Icepacks must be conditioned before packing with freeze-sensitive vaccines — conditioning is complete when ___ appear on the icepack surface and water sloshes inside.
exercises.explanation: The 2-8°C range protects vaccines from both heat (above 8°C denatures antigens) and freeze damage (below 0°C destroys adjuvant in freeze-sensitive vaccines like Pentavalent). Conditioned icepacks (at 0°C, no longer deeply frozen) prevent direct contact with sub-zero surfaces.

exercises.prompt: Match each vaccine to its open vial policy discard time.
exercises.explanation: BCG is particularly sensitive after reconstitution because the live attenuated bacteria are in suspension. MR is also a live attenuated vaccine with a 6-hour limit. OPV is uniquely allowed cold-chain return after opening.

right.text: 3 hours after reconstitution
End of session day (can be returned to cold chain)
End of session (within 6 hours of opening)
End of session day (do not return to cold chain)

exercises.prompt: A health worker finds 5 Pentavalent vials that were left outside the refrigerator overnight (room temperature 24°C). The VVM shows Stage 1. What is the correct action?
exercises.explanation:
Overnight at 24°C is a cold chain breach. VVM Stage 1 means heat exposure hasn't yet shown on the indicator, but the shake test rules out freeze damage from condensation. The vaccine focal person reviews the event; the vials may still be usable if VVM is Stage 1-2 and the cold chain breach was brief.

Why the other options are wrong: VVM Stage 1 is necessary but not sufficient after a cold chain breach. The VVM measures cumulative heat — a single overnight event might not have moved the VVM yet but the vaccines must be quarantined pending investigation and decision by a qualified person. Automatic discard wastes potentially salvageable vaccines. The correct protocol is quarantine + shake test + reporting, not immediate discard without assessment. Simply returning to the refrigerator after a breach without documentation or assessment violates cold chain protocols. The breach must be documented and investigated.

options.text: Quarantine the vials and perform the shake test — if sedimentation passes, report to vaccine focal person who will decide based on full cold chain records
Use the vials immediately since VVM Stage 1 confirms they are good
Discard all 5 vials immediately without further investigation
Return them to the refrigerator — the VVM shows they are still safe

exercises.prompt: A health facility received 200 doses of MR vaccine and administered 178 doses. Wastage rate = ___%. The Kenya MOH target wastage rate for MR is less than ___%.
exercises.explanation: Wastage = (200-178)/200 x 100 = 22/200 x 100 = 11%. Kenya MOH target for MR: < 10%. This facility is slightly above target — the vaccinator should review open vial policy compliance and session planning to reduce waste while ensuring no child is missed.

lessons.title: Community Surveillance & Outbreak Response
lessons.titleSw: Ufuatiliaji wa Afya ya Jamii na Mwitikio wa Mlipuko
lessons.briefing: Early detection of disease outbreaks saves exponentially more lives than late response. Kenya's Integrated Disease Surveillance and Response (IDSR) system gives community health workers the tools to identify unusual illness clusters, trigger alerts within 24 hours, and implement initial containment while awaiting formal public health response. Speed and systematic recording are the two critical skills.
lessons.outline: Kenya IDSR framework — priority diseases and alert thresholds; community-level detection (rumour reporting, illness clustering); 24-hour reporting obligation and the case definition; contact tracing methodology and quarantine periods; isolation vs quarantine; setting up a community isolation space; line list documentation; outbreak communication — messaging families without panic; photo capture — community health register field practice.

exercises.prompt: In a village of 300 people, a community health worker identifies 9 cases of fever and rash in the same week, all within a 500-metre radius. The background measles rate in the district is 0.5 per 100 per week. What is the village attack rate, and should an alert be triggered?
exercises.explanation:
AR = 9/300 x 100 = 3%. For measles, the IDSR threshold is any 1 suspected case (fever + generalised rash) — immediate notification is required regardless of numbers. The cluster of 9 cases makes this urgent. Notify within 24 hours.

Why the other options are wrong: IDSR does not require laboratory confirmation before alerting. Suspected cases meeting clinical criteria trigger notification. Waiting for lab delays containment. AR = 9/300 x 100 = 3%, not 0.3%. The background rate of 0.5/100 = 0.5%. The village rate (3%) is 6x higher than background — clearly above threshold. Measles affects all unvaccinated ages. The IDSR threshold is any 1 suspected case — age restriction does not apply to triggering notification.

options.text: AR = 3%; no alert yet — wait for laboratory confirmation of at least 2 cases
AR = 0.3%; below the district background rate — monitor only
AR = 3%; trigger alert only if cases are in children under 5
AR = 3% (9/300 x 100); alert threshold exceeded — any single suspected measles case triggers immediate notification

exercises.prompt: An Ebola contact must be monitored for ___ days after last exposure. A measles case is infectious from ___ days before rash onset to ___ days after rash onset.
exercises.explanation: Ebola maximum incubation is 21 days — contacts monitored for 21 days. Measles infectious period: 4 days before rash (late prodrome, highest viral shedding) to 4 days after rash appearance. This wide pre-rash infectious window is why measles spreads so rapidly before it is diagnosed.

exercises.prompt: Match each IDSR disease to its community-level alert threshold.
exercises.explanation: Alert thresholds are deliberately set low for high-consequence diseases. A single cholera case in a person over 5 is almost always epidemic cholera (El Tor) because sporadic cholera in adults is rare — any case requires immediate investigation of the water source.

right.text: Any 1 case of acute watery diarrhoea in a person over 5 years
Any 1 case of fever plus generalised rash
2 or more cases of stiff neck and fever in the same area within 1 week
2 or more deaths in the same household within 48 hours

exercises.prompt: What is the key difference between isolation and quarantine?
exercises.explanation:
Isolation removes known or suspected infectious people from the community. Quarantine monitors exposed people who may or may not become ill — duration equals the disease's maximum incubation period. Both prevent forward transmission, but the target populations are different.

Why the other options are wrong: Isolation and quarantine are not categorised by disease severity. They are defined by whether the person IS infectious (isolation) or MIGHT BECOME infectious (quarantine). Both are public health measures, not medical prescriptions. Self-isolation and self-quarantine are both valid community-level approaches with CHW monitoring. Duration varies by disease. Ebola isolation lasts until recovery/death. Measles isolation ends 4 days after rash. Quarantine period = disease-specific maximum incubation.

options.text: Isolation separates confirmed or suspected infectious cases; quarantine separates exposed but not yet symptomatic contacts for the incubation period
Isolation is used for severe cases; quarantine is for mild cases
Quarantine requires a medical prescription; isolation can be self-managed
Isolation lasts 21 days for all diseases; quarantine lasts 14 days

exercises.prompt: Visit a household in your community and complete a community health household register entry for that family. Photograph the completed register page showing at least one household member's entry with: name, age, sex, village, date of last home visit, and any current health complaint. Protect privacy — you may redact the surname.
exercises.explanation: Accurate, complete community health registers are the foundation of surveillance. A CHW who cannot maintain a register cannot detect unusual illness clusters early enough to trigger timely outbreak response.

rubric.criterion: Register page clearly photographed and readable
At least one entry includes all six required fields (name, age, sex, village, visit date, complaint)
Date of visit matches within the current week
Written reflection identifies one health concern observed in this household

lessons.title: Week 1 — Infection prevention and safe home visits
lessons.titleSw: Wiki 1 — Kuzuia maambukizi
lessons.briefing:
Community support workers reduce harm but do not diagnose beyond their competence. Before a home visit, identify the household, explain your role, obtain consent, and protect privacy. Hand hygiene follows the moments taught by health authorities: before contact, before a clean task, after body-fluid risk, after contact, and after touching surroundings.

Select PPE for the task; gloves do not replace handwashing. Never recap or transport loose needles. Clean reusable equipment between households using the approved product and contact time. Separate clean and dirty items in the field bag. Record only what is necessary and do not discuss a client in a WhatsApp group without a lawful, approved process.

Red flags—difficulty breathing, severe bleeding, altered consciousness, convulsions, chest pain, danger signs in pregnancy or a child—require urgent referral, not herbal advice or social-media diagnosis.
lessons.briefingSw: Wiki 1 — Kuzuia maambukizi: usalama, utaratibu sahihi, ukaguzi wa ubora, na huduma kwa jamii.

exercises.prompt: Which action is the safest professional starting point for infection prevention?
exercises.explanation: A competent craft worker assesses risk, scope, people, tools, and standards before starting.

options.text: Start immediately without inspecting the site or client
Assess hazards and needs, select PPE/tools, explain the plan, then begin
Copy a social-media clip without checking local conditions
Let an untrained bystander make every technical decision

exercises.prompt: What is the strongest evidence that infection prevention was completed well?
exercises.explanation: Quality is demonstrated with a repeatable inspection, measurement, or functional test.

options.text: The worker says it is fine
A documented inspection or functional test against the job specification
The cheapest material was used
The work was hidden before testing

exercises.prompt: The documented check used to prove this work meets its requirements is a quality ___.
exercises.hint: A planned check, not an opinion.
exercises.explanation: A quality audit provides evidence for the client, trainer, and next technician.

exercises.prompt: A neighbour asks you to post a patient’s wound photo in a public group to get advice. What should you do?
exercises.explanation: Community trades carry public consequences. Defects are corrected and tested, never concealed.

options.text: Continue and conceal the problem
Stop, make the area safe, explain the defect, correct it, then test and document
Ask the client to sign before seeing the work
Remove the safety device so the job appears complete

lessons.title: Week 2 — Basic observations, referral, and health promotion
lessons.titleSw: Wiki 2 — Vipimo, rufaa, na elimu
lessons.briefing:
Basic observations include temperature, pulse, breathing rate, and blood pressure only when trained and using maintained equipment. Verify identity, explain the measurement, position the person correctly, record units, repeat an unexpected result, and clean the device. A number without context is not a diagnosis.

Use approved referral pathways. State what you observed, when it began, relevant history volunteered by the client, and what first aid was given. Do not promise outcomes. Health promotion should be practical and respectful: safe water, immunisation information, nutrition, mosquito control, medication adherence, maternal danger signs, and clinic follow-up.

Safeguarding concerns involving children, vulnerable adults, violence, or exploitation follow the institution’s escalation policy. Do not investigate alone or confront a suspected abuser in a way that increases danger.

lessons.title: Week 4 — Bookkeeping, profit, cash flow, and break-even
lessons.titleSw: Wiki 4 — Vitabu, faida, cash flow, na break-even
lessons.briefing:
Use separate business money. Record every sale, purchase, expense, owner contribution, withdrawal, amount owed by customers (receivables), and amount owed to suppliers (payables). Keep source documents: invoice, receipt, M-Pesa/bank statement, delivery note, payroll record. Reconcile the cashbook to actual cash and the mobile/bank statement; differences are investigated, not forced into “miscellaneous”.

Profit is not cash. Income statement: revenue minus cost of sales gives gross profit; minus operating expenses gives net profit. A profitable business can fail when customers pay in 60 days but suppliers demand cash today. A cash-flow forecast places expected receipts and payments in the week/month they occur. Opening cash + inflows − outflows = closing cash. VAT or other tax collected is not the owner’s profit; keep it separate according to current KRA obligations and obtain qualified advice.

Contribution per unit = selling price − variable cost. Break-even units = fixed costs ÷ contribution per unit. Example: a welding shop charges KES 6,000 for a standard grill; steel, rods, paint, and direct piece labour are KES 3,500. Contribution is KES 2,500. If monthly fixed costs are KES 100,000, break-even is 40 grills. Below 40 the model loses money; above it each additional grill contributes KES 2,500 before tax and unusual costs.

Gross margin percentage = gross profit ÷ revenue × 100. Markup is profit ÷ cost; it is not the same. Price also includes waste, warranty/rework, payment fees, bad debts, and tool depreciation. Close books monthly: stock count, receivables age, supplier reconciliation, bank reconciliation, income statement, and next 13 weeks of cash.
lessons.briefingSw: Tenganisha pesa ya biashara. Rekodi mauzo, gharama, drawings, receivables na payables. Profit si cash. Contribution = bei minus variable cost. Break-even = fixed costs / contribution. Reconcile cashbook na bank/M-Pesa. Tax si faida.
