It sweeps carrier frequency across a wide bandwidth, allowing mathematical correlators to decode packets even when signal strength is 20 dB below background noise

exercises.prompt: Meshtastic private group channels are encrypted using the industry-standard ___ symmetric encryption cipher to prevent unauthorized eavesdropping on the open airwaves.
exercises.explanation: Meshtastic supports AES-256 bit symmetric key encryption. Sharing the encryption key securely (via offline QR code or secure transfer) allows private group communications that cannot be read by other mesh participants.

exercises.prompt: Match each Meshtastic mesh networking element to its role.

right.text: Handheld radio connected via Bluetooth to a smartphone for text messaging
Autonomous solar-powered radio on a high vantage point to relay packets
Prevents packets from bouncing indefinitely in infinite loops across the mesh
License-exempt frequency band allocated for digital packet radio in ITU Region 1

lessons.title: Antenna Masts, Lightning & Grounding
lessons.titleSw: Minara ya Antena, Radi na Upimaji wa Earth
lessons.briefing:
In radio communications, antenna elevation is power: elevating an antenna from 2 meters
to 10 meters above ground quadruples your operational VHF line-of-sight range. However,
erecting an elevated metal mast in thunderstorm-prone regions of East Africa (such as
the Lake Victoria basin, which experiences over 200 thunderstorm days annually) creates
an enormous lightning strike hazard. Connecting an ungrounded mast to indoor radio equipment
invites catastrophic fire, equipment destruction, and fatal electric shock. This final
day covers radio horizon trigonometry, guyed mast engineering (bamboo and conduit),
coaxial cable attenuation physics, and single-point RF lightning grounding standards.
lessons.briefingSw:
Kuinua antena juu kutoka mita 2 hadi mita 10 huongeza umbali wa mawasiliano mara nne.
Lakini ukiinua mnara bila kuweka earth ya kuzuia radi katika maeneo yenye radi nyingi
kama Ziwa Victoria, unakaribisha moto na ajali mbaya. Siku hii inafundisha jinsi ya
kujenga mnara wa mianzi au chuma ulioshikiliwa kwa nyaya tatu (guy wires) na kuweka
mfumo salama wa earth na kuzuia radi.
lessons.outline:
1. The radio horizon equation: Calculating line-of-sight distance (D = 3.57 * (sqrt(h1) + sqrt(h2)))
2. Improvised antenna masts: Cured bamboo vs galvanized steel electrical conduit (EMT)
3. The 3-way guy wire geometry: 120-degree radial triangulation with earth screw anchors
4. Coaxial cable attenuation: RG-58 vs RG-213 vs LMR-400 (decibel signal loss per 10 meters)
5. The RF Choke (Ugly Balun): Coiling coaxial cable to suppress common-mode outer-shield currents
6. Lightning physics: Step potential, side-flashing, and induced electromagnetic pulse (EMP)
7. Single-point grounding: Coaxial gas discharge arrestors, 16 mm² copper wire, and 2.4m earth rods
8. PHOTO_CAPTURE practical: Construct and document an antenna build or RF grounding installation

exercises.prompt: An operator connects a 433 MHz LoRa transceiver to an antenna mounted on a 30-meter tall mast using thin RG-58 coaxial cable. Testing shows almost no signal reaching the next node. Why?
exercises.explanation:
Correct! High-frequency UHF signals (433 MHz) suffer massive dielectric and resistive losses in thin cables. A 9.2 dB loss leaves less than 12% of transmitter power reaching the antenna. High-grade low-loss cable (like LMR-400 or RG-213) must be used for UHF runs exceeding 5 meters.

Why the other options are wrong: There is no indication of physical lightning damage. All radio frequencies travel through properly rated coaxial transmission lines. Earth's magnetic field does not attenuate RF signals inside coaxial cables.

options.text: The radio was struck by lightning during installation
UHF radio waves cannot travel through coaxial cables
The earth's magnetic field cancels out vertical cable runs
RG-58 cable suffers extreme attenuation (~9.2 dB loss per 30m at 433 MHz), which dissipates over 88% of the radio's power as heat before it reaches the antenna

exercises.prompt: When installing a heavy copper lightning downlead conductor from an antenna mast to the ground rod, you must avoid sharp ___ degree bends because high-frequency lightning energy will arc off the corner.
exercises.explanation: Lightning discharges contain high-frequency impulse currents where sharp bends create high inductive reactance. The lightning surge will jump (side-flash) directly off a sharp 90-degree corner rather than following the wire into the ground rod.

exercises.prompt: Practical Assessment: Document your field antenna construction, coaxial connection, or RF lightning grounding installation.

rubric.criterion: Antenna element or ground system constructed according to engineering specifications (dipole, ground plane, or mast grounding downlead)
Coaxial connector (SO-239, BNC, SMA, or PL-259) soldered or crimped cleanly with weatherproofing wrap
Measurement scale (ruler/tape measure) visible confirming calculated resonant element lengths
Written or verbal caption explaining the target frequency (e.g. 145 MHz VHF or 868 MHz LoRa) and calculated quarter-wavelength
Photo clearly displays the fully assembled field setup with handwritten student callsign/ID and date visible

lessons.title: Haemorrhage Control & Tourniquet Application
lessons.titleSw: Udhibiti wa Kutoka Damu na Utumiaji wa Tourniquet
lessons.briefing:
Uncontrolled haemorrhage is the leading cause of preventable death in trauma —
responsible for 30–40% of all trauma fatalities globally, and the majority of
battlefield and road-traffic-accident deaths that occur before hospital arrival.
In Kenya, where an EMS ambulance in rural areas can take 60–90 minutes or never
arrive, bystander haemorrhage control is a literal life-or-death skill. This day
teaches the physiology of blood loss, the three-step haemorrhage control hierarchy,
correct tourniquet application, and wound packing with improvised materials.
lessons.briefingSw:
Kutoka damu bila kudhibitiwa ndiyo sababu kuu ya vifo vinavyoweza kuzuiwa katika
majeraha — inawajibika kwa asilimia 30–40 ya vifo vyote vya majeraha duniani.
Nchini Kenya, ambapo ambulensi ya EMS katika maeneo ya vijijini inaweza kuchukua
dakika 60–90, udhibiti wa kutoka damu na watu wa kawaida ni ujuzi wa kweli wa
kuokoa maisha.
lessons.outline:
1. Blood loss physiology: classes of haemorrhage (I–IV) and their clinical signs
2. The haemorrhage control hierarchy: direct pressure → wound packing → tourniquet
3. Direct pressure: technique, duration, and when to escalate
4. Wound packing: improvised materials, packing technique, haemostatic agents
5. Tourniquet anatomy: commercial CAT/SOFTT-W vs improvised windlass tourniquet
6. Tourniquet application: limb selection, placement, tightening, time recording
7. Tourniquet myths debunked: ischaemia time, limb loss, when NOT to remove
8. Junctional wounds (groin, axilla, neck): pressure and improvised approaches

exercises.prompt: A road accident patient has a deep thigh laceration with pulsatile bleeding. You apply direct pressure with your shirt for 3 minutes — blood soaks through and is pooling rapidly. What is the correct next step?
exercises.explanation:
Correct. Pulsatile bleeding is arterial. A deep thigh laceration with arterial bleeding that overwhelms direct pressure in 3 minutes indicates Class II–III haemorrhage. This is a clear tourniquet indication. Apply high and tight if exact wound extent is unclear.

Why the other options are wrong: Removing the soaked dressing disrupts the early clot forming at the wound base. Add fresh material on top of the soaked shirt. More importantly, pulsatile arterial bleeding from a deep thigh wound has already failed direct pressure — escalate to wound packing or tourniquet. Calling for help is important but does not stop bleeding. In rural Kenya, EMS may be 60+ minutes away. A patient losing 250 mL/minute from an arterial thigh wound will be in Class IV cardiac arrest within 8–10 minutes without intervention. Elevation reduces venous pressure but has minimal effect on arterial haemorrhage. The femoral artery runs at nearly aortic pressure — elevation will not control pulsatile arterial bleeding from a thigh laceration.

options.text: Remove the soaked shirt, replace with fresh material, and continue direct pressure for another 10 minutes
Call an ambulance and wait — moving the patient may worsen the bleeding
Elevate the leg above heart level to reduce blood pressure at the wound
Apply an improvised tourniquet 5–7 cm above the wound immediately — pulsatile arterial bleeding from the thigh that has soaked through direct pressure is life-threatening

exercises.prompt: After applying a tourniquet, you must record the time of application on the patient's ___ using a marker or blood so the receiving hospital knows how long it has been in place.
exercises.explanation: Time of tourniquet application (written as 'TK HH:MM') on the forehead is the international standard. The forehead is always visible, not covered by clothing or dressings, and survives transport. It allows any receiving clinician to immediately calculate ischaemia time.

exercises.prompt: Match each haemorrhage class to its characteristic signs and appropriate first aid response.

right.text: Normal vitals, mild anxiety — direct pressure sufficient
HR > 100, anxiety, decreased pulse pressure — pressure + packing
HR > 120, low BP, confusion — tourniquet + urgent evacuation
Unconscious, no BP — immediate tourniquet; near-fatal without surgery

lessons.title: Airway & Breathing Management
lessons.titleSw: Usimamizi wa Njia ya Hewa na Kupumua
lessons.briefing:
An occluded airway causes irreversible brain damage in 4 to 6 minutes and death
shortly after. In trauma, unconsciousness allows the tongue to fall backward against
the pharyngeal wall, producing complete mechanical airway obstruction. In road
traffic crashes and falls, cervical spine trauma must be assumed, meaning standard
head-tilt chin-lift maneuvers can cause quadriplegia. This day teaches manual airway
maneuvers (jaw-thrust vs head-tilt), recovery position, tension pneumothorax
recognition, chest seals for sucking chest wounds, and rescue breathing protocols.
lessons.briefingSw:
Njia ya hewa iliyoziba husababisha uharibifu wa kudumu wa ubongo ndani ya dakika 4
hadi 6 na kifo baada ya muda mfupi. Katika majeraha, kupoteza fahamu huruhusu ulimi
kuanguka nyuma na kuzuia njia ya hewa. Siku hii inafundisha mbinu za kufungua njia
ya hewa kwa mikono (jaw-thrust vs head-tilt), mkao wa kurejesha fahamu (recovery position),
na matibabu ya jeraha la kifua.
lessons.outline:
1. Anatomy of upper airway obstruction: the tongue, foreign bodies, secretions, and blood
2. Suspected spinal injury: Jaw-Thrust maneuver vs non-trauma Head-Tilt Chin-Lift
3. Airway clearance: digital sweep precautions, suction, and postural drainage
4. The Recovery Position (lateral recumbent): biomechanics and step-by-step procedure
5. Sucking chest wounds (open pneumothorax): pathophysiology and 3-sided occlusive dressings
6. Tension pneumothorax red flags: tracheal deviation, unilateral breath sounds, jugular distension
7. Rescue breathing and hands-only CPR fundamentals for adult bystanders
8. Choking protocols (Heimlich abdominal thrusts and back blows in conscious vs unconscious)

exercises.prompt: You arrive at a motorcycle crash scene. The driver is unresponsive, lying on their back, making gurgling/snoring respirations. How should you open their airway?
exercises.explanation:
Correct. Jaw-thrust displaces the mandible and tongue forward without moving the cervical spine, protecting against secondary spinal cord injury.

Why the other options are wrong: Head-tilt hyperextends the cervical vertebrae. In a vehicular crash, cervical fracture must be assumed; hyperextension risks spinal cord transection. Blind finger sweeps can push foreign bodies or broken teeth deeper into the larynx, converting a partial obstruction into a complete one. Sitting an unconscious trauma patient upright collapses airway tone further and endangers an un-stabilized spine.

options.text: Apply a vigorous Head-Tilt Chin-Lift to maximize airway diameter
Immediately force the mouth open and execute a blind finger sweep
Perform a modified Jaw-Thrust while maintaining head and neck in neutral alignment
Sit the patient upright and slap their back

exercises.prompt: When improvising an occlusive dressing for a penetrating sucking chest wound, you should tape down ___ sides of the plastic wrapper to create a flutter valve.
exercises.explanation: Taping three sides creates a one-way flutter valve: it blocks air entry during inhalation while allowing trapped air and blood to vent out the open fourth side during exhalation, preventing tension pneumothorax.

exercises.prompt: Match each respiratory trauma condition to its primary emergency intervention.

right.text: Lateral recovery position to enable gravitational drainage

left.text: Penetrating chest wound with bubbling blood

right.text: 3-sided vented occlusive dressing

left.text: Traumatic cardiac arrest (no pulse, no breathing)

right.text: High-quality chest compressions at 100-120 bpm, 5-6 cm depth

left.text: Conscious adult with complete airway obstruction

right.text: Alternating 5 back blows and 5 abdominal thrusts (Heimlich)

lessons.title: Burns, Scalds & Wound Care
lessons.titleSw: Kuungua, Kuchemka na Utunzaji wa Majeraha
lessons.briefing:
Burns cause catastrophic fluid loss, hypothermia, excruciating pain, and overwhelming
systemic sepsis. In East Africa, open cookfires, overturned paraffin lamps, and hot tea/boiling
water scalds account for thousands of pediatric trauma admissions annually. Harmful
traditional remedies (applying raw eggs, motor oil, toothpaste, cow dung) trigger
devastating bacterial infections and tissue necrosis. This day teaches the Rule of Nines
depth classification, correct thermal cooling protocols, clean covering methods, fluid
resuscitation basics (Parkland formula), and antiseptic wound irrigation.
lessons.briefingSw:
Kuungua husababisha upotevu mkubwa wa maji mwilini, hypothermia, maumivu makali,
na maambukizi ya hatari (sepsis). Katika Afrika Mashariki, majiko ya kuni, taa za
mafuta ya taa, na chai moto husababisha majeraha mengi kwa watoto. Dawa za kienyeji
zenye madhara kama kupaka yai, mafuta ya gari, au mchanga huleta maambukizi makali.
Siku hii inafundisha kanuni sahihi za kutuliza kwa maji baridi na kufunika jeraha.
lessons.outline:
1. Burn depth classification: superficial (1st), partial thickness (2nd), full thickness (3rd)
2. Total Body Surface Area (TBSA) estimation: Wallace Rule of Nines and the Palmar Method
3. Immediate emergency action: Stop the burning process, remove constricting jewellery
4. Cooling protocol: clean cool running water for 20 minutes (never ice or freezing water)
5. What NEVER to put on a burn: debunking toothpaste, eggs, flour, cow dung, and engine oil
6. Dressing and protection: plastic cling film wrap vs sterile non-adherent sheets
7. Fluid loss & shock: oral rehydration therapy (ORT) vs intravenous Ringer's Lactate
8. Wound irrigation: high-pressure saline flushing vs soaking, signs of wound infection (cellulitis)

exercises.prompt: A child suffers boiling water scalds across their entire chest, abdomen, and the front of one arm. Using the Rule of Nines, what is the estimated TBSA?
exercises.explanation:
Correct! Entire anterior torso (chest 9% + abdomen 9% = 18%) plus anterior surface of one arm (4.5%) = 22.5% TBSA. This represents major pediatric burn trauma requiring IV fluids.

Why the other options are wrong: Chest alone is 9%. Abdomen is another 9%. The anterior arm is 4.5%. 36% would include both sides of the torso. This underestimates the combined chest and abdominal surface area.

exercises.prompt: Burns should be cooled with clean running water for exactly ___ minutes to halt heat progression without causing hypothermia.
exercises.explanation: Clinical guidelines worldwide (ANZBA, British Burn Association) mandate 20 minutes of cool running water. Shorter durations fail to dissipate deep thermal energy, while using ice causes vasoconstriction and tissue necrosis.

exercises.prompt: Match each burn intervention to its rationale.

right.text: Excludes atmospheric air to cut nerve pain and prevents adherence

left.text: Immediate removal of rings and bracelets

right.text: Prevents ischemic necrosis from progressive tissue oedema
Prevents reactive vasoconstriction and systemic hypothermia
Flushes bacteria and necrotic debris from contaminated lacerations

lessons.title: Fractures, Dislocations & Improvised Splinting
lessons.titleSw: Mifupa Iliyovunjika, Kutoka na Splinting ya Kubuni
lessons.briefing:
Unstabilised fractures cause severe pain, vascular transection, fat embolism syndrome,
and convert closed fractures into contaminated open wounds during bumpy rural transport.
A fractured femur can bleed 1.5 to 2.0 litres of blood into the thigh compartment silently.
This day teaches fracture classification, the PMS (Pulse, Motor, Sensory) neurovascular
assessment algorithm, the golden rule of splinting (immobilising the joint above and below),
and practical improvised splints built from sticks, cardboard, blankets, and triangular bandages.
lessons.briefingSw:
Mifupa iliyovunjika isipowekewa splint husababisha maumivu makali, uharibifu wa mishipa
ya damu, na kuvuja kwa damu kwa ndani (mfupa wa paja unaweza kupoteza lita 1.5–2 za damu).
Siku hii inafundisha jinsi ya kutambua mivunjiko, ukaguzi wa PMS (Mapigo ya moyo, Mwendo,
na Hisia), na mbinu za kutengeneza splint kwa kutumia miti, makadibodi, na kanga.
lessons.outline:
1. Fracture classifications: closed vs open (compound), greenstick, comminuted
2. The PMS check: Pulse, Motor function, and Sensory assessment before and after splinting
3. The Golden Rule of Splinting: immobilise one joint above and one joint below the fracture
4. Open fracture emergency management: sterile covering, no bone reduction into wound
5. Improvised splinting materials: branches, timber slats, folded cardboard, rolled blankets
6. Traction splinting concepts for mid-shaft femur fractures (anatomical splinting)
7. Sling and swathe techniques for collarbone (clavicle) and shoulder dislocations
8. Compartment syndrome recognition: the 5 Ps (Pain out of proportion, Pallor, Pulselessness, Paresthesia, Paralysis)

exercises.prompt: You apply an improvised cardboard splint to a patient's fractured lower leg. Five minutes later, the patient complains their foot feels numb and you can no longer feel the dorsalis pedis pulse. What should you do immediately?
exercises.explanation:
Correct! Disappearance of a pulse or onset of numbness post-splinting indicates mechanical vascular or nerve compression by the splint ties. Loosen the bandages immediately until pulses return.

Why the other options are wrong: Elevation will not restore a mechanically compressed arterial supply and may worsen ischemia. Waiting risks permanent nerve damage and ischemic muscle death. Ischemia must be relieved immediately. Tightening further will completely occlude remaining collateral circulation, causing gangrene.

options.text: Elevate the leg higher to decrease swelling
Loosen the splint wraps and re-check the distal pulse and sensation
Wait 30 minutes to see if circulation normalizes
Tighten the ties further to secure the bone fragments

exercises.prompt: The golden rule of fracture management dictates that a splint must immobilise the joint ___ and the joint ___ the fracture site.
exercises.explanation: Immobilising both the joint above and the joint below prevents muscular contraction and rotational forces from displacing the fractured bone ends.

exercises.prompt: Match each type of improvised splint to its ideal clinical application.

right.text: Binding the injured leg to the uninjured leg with padding between knees and ankles
Immobilising clavicle fractures and dislocated shoulders against the chest wall
Rapid rigid immobilisation of forearm, wrist, or lower leg fractures
Bilateral lateral/medial splinting for remote wilderness long-bone fractures

lessons.title: Patient Assessment & Improvised Evacuation
lessons.titleSw: Tathmini ya Mgonjwa na Uokoaji wa Kubuni
lessons.briefing:
In disaster response and remote trauma incidents, the greatest danger to the casualty
often occurs during rough, uncoordinated evacuation. Dropping a casualty, twisting an
unstable cervical spine, or attempting single-rescuer drag carries can prove fatal.
This final day unites everything into a systematic Primary & Secondary Survey
(<C>ABCDE algorithm), simple triage color coding, and practical construction of improvised
stretchers using everyday materials: two poles with blankets, jackets, or sacks.
lessons.briefingSw:
Katika majanga na majeraha ya vijijini, hatari kubwa mara nyingi hutokea wakati wa
usafirishaji wa haraka usioratibiwa. Siku hii ya mwisho inakamilisha mfumo mzima wa
tathmini ya mgonjwa kwa utaratibu wa <C>ABCDE, mbinu za triage, na jinsi ya kutengeneza
machela imara ya kubuni kwa kutumia miti miwili na kanga, koti, au magunia.
lessons.outline:
1. Scene safety and sizing up: hazards (electrical, fire, traffic, toxic gas)
2. The <C>ABCDE Trauma Algorithm: Catastrophic Bleeding, Airway, Breathing, Circulation, Disability, Exposure
3. Rapid Trauma Assessment (Head-to-toe DCAP-BTLS survey)
4. START Simple Triage: Green (Walking Wounded), Yellow (Delayed), Red (Immediate), Black (Expectant)
5. Mechanics of lifting: protecting the rescuer's spine and coordinating multi-bearer moves
6. Improvised stretcher designs: Blanket & Poles, Button-Shirt / Jacket Sleeves, Burlap/Sisal Sacks
7. Loading and securing a casualty onto a stretcher: Log-roll with manual in-line spinal stabilization
8. PHOTO_CAPTURE practical: Construct and document an improvised load-bearing stretcher

exercises.prompt: Under the <C>ABCDE trauma protocol, why is catastrophic external bleeding assessed and treated BEFORE managing the airway?
exercises.explanation:
Correct! Catastrophic arterial bleeding causes exsanguination and irreversible shock in 2–3 minutes. Controlling active massive hemorrhage (<C>) takes immediate priority before airway interventions.

Why the other options are wrong: Airway is always vital, but massive arterial haemorrhage causes fatal hypovolemic cardiac arrest faster than airway occlusion. Prioritisation is strictly dictated by physiological survival timelines, not technical ease. Opening an airway restores oxygenation and does not artificially spike blood pressure.

options.text: Because an open airway is not important if the patient is unconscious
Bleeding control is technically easier than opening the airway
A patient with complete femoral artery transection can bleed to death in under 3 minutes, outstripping the timeline of hypoxic brain damage
Airway interventions always increase blood pressure, which worsens bleeding

exercises.prompt: In the START triage system, casualties who are breathing, have a radial pulse, but are unable to walk due to a closed femur fracture are classified under the color category ___ (Delayed).
exercises.explanation: Yellow (Delayed / P2) indicates casualties with significant injuries who have stable vitals (normal respirations and perfusion) and can safely wait until all Red (Immediate) casualties are evacuated.

exercises.prompt: Practical Assessment: Build and test an improvised load-bearing stretcher.

rubric.criterion: Two rigid longitudinal poles (wood, bamboo, metal pipe ≥ 2m long) used as the frame
Fabric bed constructed using Blanket-wrap, Jacket-sleeves, or Sack-feed method
Tested with a test subject or heavy load (≥ 50 kg) showing no slippage or tear
Photo clearly displays the fully assembled stretcher with test weight loaded
Written or verbal description explaining the friction or locking mechanism utilized

lessons.title: Hermetic Grain Storage: Keeping Maize & Legumes Safe
lessons.titleSw: Uhifadhi wa Nafaka kwa Hermetic: Kulinda Mahindi na Mikunde
lessons.briefing: Kenya loses 30–40 % of its grain harvest every year to weevils, moulds, and rodents — before the food ever reaches a family. Hermetic (airtight) storage kills insects without chemicals by starving them of oxygen. This day teaches you to select, prepare, fill, and seal hermetic bags and metal silos using materials available in most Kenyan markets.
lessons.briefingSw: Kenya hupoteza asilimia 30–40 ya mavuno yake ya nafaka kila mwaka kutokana na wadudu, ukungu, na panya — kabla chakula haijafika kwa familia. Uhifadhi wa hermetic huua wadudu bila kemikali kwa kuwanyima oksijeni.
lessons.outline:
1. Why grain rots: the post-harvest loss triangle (moisture, insects, fungi)
2. Hermetic principle: O₂ depletion and CO₂ build-up kill weevils in 7–14 days
3. PICS bags vs. triple-layer hermetic bags vs. metal silos — cost and capacity
4. Moisture testing: bite test, 105 °C oven method, and affordable moisture meters
5. Filling, sealing, and stacking — avoiding puncture failure
6. Aflatoxin risk: visual sorting and UV lamp inspection
7. Rodent-proofing: silo placement, pallet rules, cat/trap programmes
8. Opening safely: airing before re-entry into enclosed stores

exercises.prompt: A farmer bites a dried maize kernel and it bends without snapping. What should she do?
exercises.explanation:
Correct. The grain needs further drying. Retest after 2–3 days of open sun-drying on a tarpaulin, ideally on a raised rack.

Why the other options are wrong: Bending without snapping signals moisture above ~14 %. Hermetic storage will trap that moisture and cause explosive mould. Silica gel can help reduce residual humidity in very small quantities but cannot compensate for wet grain — it would be overwhelmed in hours. An open bag is no longer hermetic. It provides no O₂ depletion effect and leaves grain exposed to insects.

options.text: Fill the hermetic bags immediately — the grain is ready
Continue sun-drying for 2–3 more days then retest
Add silica gel sachets inside the hermetic bag to absorb moisture
Store immediately but leave the bag slightly open to allow ventilation

exercises.prompt: Hermetic storage kills insects by depleting ___ below 2% inside the sealed container.
exercises.explanation: As grain and insects respire, O₂ is consumed and CO₂ builds up. Below ~2% O₂, all insect life stages (egg, larva, pupa, adult) die within 7–14 days.

exercises.prompt: Match each storage technology to its primary advantage.

right.text: Low-cost, widely available, reusable 2–4 seasons
Rodent-proof, 20+ year lifespan, best for community stores
UV-stabilised for outdoor stacking, suits 50–1 000 kg
No hermetic benefit — weevils freely enter and exit

exercises.prompt: A UV torch shows blue-green glow on some groundnuts. What is the correct action?
exercises.explanation:
UV fluorescence indicates Aspergillus mould. Destroy by burying deeply or burning. Never feed aflatoxin-contaminated grain to any animal.

Why the other options are wrong: Aflatoxin accumulates in poultry liver and eggs. Contaminated eggs enter the human food chain. Do not feed to any livestock. Aflatoxin is bound to the grain matrix and is not water-soluble. Washing has no effect. Fluorescence persists as long as the mould is present. It does not fade and the toxin does not break down at room temperature.

options.text: Remove glowing nuts and feed them to chickens — the toxin is less harmful to poultry
Wash glowing nuts with clean water to remove the toxin
Remove and destroy glowing nuts; do not consume or feed to animals
Continue storage — UV glow only appears during the first days and disappears

lessons.title: Solar Drying: Fish, Fruits, and Vegetables
lessons.titleSw: Ukaushaji wa Jua: Samaki, Matunda, na Mboga
lessons.briefing: Sun-drying reduces water activity in food from ~0.99 to below 0.60, making it impossible for bacteria, moulds, and yeasts to grow. Done correctly, solar drying preserves fish for 6–12 months and fruits/vegetables for 3–6 months without electricity or refrigeration. This day covers dryer design, pre-treatment chemistry, and the critical hygiene practices that prevent contamination.
lessons.briefingSw: Ukaushaji wa jua hupunguza shughuli ya maji katika chakula kutoka ~0.99 hadi chini ya 0.60, na kuifanya kuwa haiwezekani kwa bakteria, ukungu, na chachu kukua. Ikifanywa vizuri, ukaushaji wa jua huhifadhi samaki kwa miezi 6–12.
lessons.outline:
1. Water activity (Aᵥ) and microbial safety thresholds
2. Open-air vs. raised-rack vs. solar tunnel dryer — efficiency comparison
3. Solar tunnel dryer construction: materials, dimensions, ventilation
4. Pre-treatment: salting, blanching, lemon/ascorbic acid, sulphiting
5. Slicing geometry and surface-area-to-mass ratio
6. Fish drying: gutting, brining, fly control (muslin netting)
7. Dryness test and packaging for long storage
8. Rehydration and nutritional retention data

exercises.prompt: A community dryer has 200 kg of fresh tilapia. After 3 days of solar drying the batch weighs 58 kg. Is this expected?
exercises.explanation:
Correct. Fish loses 70–75 % of its fresh weight on drying. The dried product is nutrient-dense: 58 kg of dried omena contains the protein of ~230 kg fresh.

Why the other options are wrong: Fresh fish is ~ 75 % water. A 75 % mass reduction from 200 kg yields 50 kg. 58 kg (71 % reduction) is within normal range — well-dried fish. A 30 % loss would mean 140 kg remaining — that fish would be dangerously wet (Aᵥ > 0.90) and would spoil within days. The weight loss is driven by the water content of the fish, not by dryer efficiency. Solar tunnel efficiency affects speed, not final mass.

options.text: No — too much weight lost; the fish has been over-dried and is ruined
No — losses should be less than 30 %; something went wrong
Yes — fresh fish is ~75 % water; 50–60 kg output from 200 kg fresh is normal
Yes — but only because the solar tunnel is more efficient than expected

exercises.prompt: Blanching vegetables in boiling water for 2–4 minutes before solar drying deactivates ___ that cause browning.
exercises.explanation: Peroxidase and polyphenol oxidase are heat-labile enzymes responsible for enzymatic browning. Blanching denatures them, preserving the product's colour and extending shelf life.

exercises.prompt: A single blow-fly lands on fresh fish in the solar dryer for one hour before the muslin cover is replaced. What is the risk?
exercises.explanation:
Correct. Inspect immediately. If eggs are visible (tiny white rice-grain specks), remove and discard that portion of flesh. Cover the remaining product and continue drying.

Why the other options are wrong: A single Calliphora or Lucilia female can lay 200–300 eggs in a single batch. At 35 °C eggs hatch in 6–8 hours into maggots that penetrate flesh rapidly. Blow-flies deposit eggs directly on protein-rich surfaces. Bacterial contamination is secondary; the primary concern is larval infestation. Tunnel temperatures reach 50–70 °C at the black base but the fish surface where eggs are laid may be cooler. Eggs are also relatively heat-tolerant in the first hours.

options.text: Negligible — one fly cannot lay enough eggs to cause visible damage
Moderate — flies only contaminate fish with bacteria, not eggs
None — the high temperature inside the solar tunnel kills eggs on contact
Serious — blow-fly eggs can hatch within 6–8 hours; the exposed fish should be inspected and the affected area removed

lessons.title: Lacto-Fermentation: Uji, Fermented Milk, and Vegetables
lessons.titleSw: Kuchacha kwa Lacto: Uji, Maziwa Yaliyochachushwa, na Mboga
lessons.briefing: Lacto-fermentation is one of humanity's oldest food technologies — and one of the most powerful. Lactic acid bacteria (LAB) convert sugars to lactic acid, dropping pH below 4.0 and making food microbiologically safe without heat or refrigeration. In Kenya, fermented foods (uji wa togwa, mursik, fermented cassava) underpin everyday nutrition. This day decodes the microbiology and teaches safe, controlled fermentation of grains, dairy, and vegetables.
lessons.briefingSw: Kuchacha kwa lacto ni moja ya teknolojia za zamani zaidi za chakula cha binadamu — na moja ya zenye nguvu zaidi. Bakteria ya asidi ya lactic (LAB) hubadilisha sukari kuwa asidi ya lactic, kupunguza pH chini ya 4.0 na kufanya chakula kuwa salama bila joto wala jokofu.
lessons.outline:
1. Lactic acid bacteria (LAB): species, substrates, and environments
2. pH drop as a preservation mechanism — the 4.0 barrier
3. Uji wa togwa: sorghum/maize fermentation protocol (48–72 hours)
4. Mursik: traditional Kalenjin fermented milk — the gourd process
5. Vegetable fermentation: salt concentration, brine ratios, and anaerobic sealing
6. Fermented cassava (kivunde/gari): detoxification of hydrogen cyanide
7. Probiotic benefits: LAB and gut health evidence
8. Failure modes and how to recognise unsafe ferments

exercises.prompt: A batch of fermented uji smells strongly of alcohol after 72 hours but has no sour taste. pH strips show pH 5.8. What happened and what should you do?
exercises.explanation:
Correct. Yeast fermentation produces ethanol and CO₂ but does not acidify effectively. At pH 5.8, Salmonella and E. coli can still survive. Start a new batch with back-slopping culture from a reliable source.

Why the other options are wrong: Lactic fermentation produces a clean sour smell, not an alcohol odour. Dominant alcohol at 72 hours indicates yeast, not LAB, are in control. Alcohol does have antimicrobial properties at high concentrations (> 10 % ABV) but the small amounts in a fermented slurry are insufficient. pH 5.8 is above the 4.6 safety threshold for botulism prevention. Adding more substrate feeds the yeast further. The vessel is already contaminated with yeast. Clean the vessel, sterilise with boiling water, and start fresh.

options.text: Normal — uji always smells of alcohol in the first 72 hours. Continue fermentation for 24 more hours.
Safe to consume — alcohol is a natural preservative and the pH of 5.8 is acceptable
Yeasts outcompeted LAB — fermentation is alcoholic, not lactic. Discard the batch; pH 5.8 is not safe for pathogen inhibition.
Add more flour to dilute the alcohol and restart fermentation

exercises.prompt: The minimum safe pH for lacto-fermented food — below which *Clostridium botulinum* cannot produce toxin — is ___.
exercises.explanation: C. botulinum produces botulinum toxin (one of the most lethal biological substances known) only in anaerobic environments above pH 4.6. Lacto-fermentation targets pH ≤ 4.0 — well within the safe zone.

exercises.prompt: Match each fermented food to its primary LAB species and region.

right.text: Lactobacillus fermentum + L. plantarum — sorghum/maize gruel
Lactococcus lactis — smoked gourd fermented milk
Leuconostoc mesenteroides → L. plantarum — shredded cabbage, 5% salt
Mixed LAB — fermented, pressed, and toasted cassava flour

lessons.title: Salt & Smoke Preservation: Meat, Fish, and Hides
lessons.titleSw: Uhifadhi wa Chumvi na Moshi: Nyama, Samaki, na Ngozi
lessons.briefing: Before refrigeration, salt and smoke preserved the meat and fish that fed civilisations across millennia. Combined correctly, they reduce water activity, inhibit enzymatic spoilage, and deposit antimicrobial phenolic compounds from smoke. This day teaches the biochemistry and practical protocols for dry salting, brine curing, and hot/cold smoking — applicable to goat, beef, fish, and even hides for leather.
lessons.briefingSw: Kabla ya jokofu, chumvi na moshi vilihifadhi nyama na samaki ambavyo vililisha ustaarabu kwa milenia. Ikijumuishwa vizuri, hupunguza shughuli ya maji, kuzuia uharibifu wa enzymes, na kuweka misombo ya antimicrobial kutoka kwa moshi.
lessons.outline:
1. Mechanisms: Aᵥ reduction by salt, phenolic deposition by smoke
2. Dry salting vs. wet brine curing — applications and ratios
3. Nitrite curing (sodium nitrate/nitrite) — the botulism connection
4. Hot smoking: temperature, time, and wood species
5. Cold smoking: temperature control and extended shelf life
6. Building a field smokehouse from clay, bricks, or sheet metal
7. Charqui / biltong / nyama choma wa kukaushwa: combined salt-dry method
8. Rancidity prevention: antioxidants and packaging

exercises.prompt: You are hot-smoking tilapia in a barrel smoker. After 3 hours the chamber temperature has been steady at 85 °C. You probe the thickest fish and read 58 °C. What should you do?
exercises.explanation:
Correct. Pathogen kill is based on the cold-point temperature inside the thickest piece, not the chamber. Continue smoking and verify with the probe before removing.

Why the other options are wrong: Fish must reach 63 °C internal temperature for 15 minutes, or 70 °C for 2 minutes, to kill Listeria and Salmonella. 58 °C is below the safety threshold regardless of chamber temperature. Chamber temperature and internal temperature are different. Thick fish can remain under-temperature for hours in a hot chamber. Internal probe measurement is mandatory for food safety. At 120 °C the fish surface will burn and dry out before the interior reaches temperature. Maintain 70–90 °C and allow adequate time.

options.text: Remove the fish immediately — 58 °C is adequate and further cooking will dry them out too much
The chamber temperature is sufficient — internal temperature does not need to be measured for fish
Continue smoking until the internal temperature reaches at least 63 °C, then hold for 15 minutes
Add more fuel to raise chamber temperature to 120 °C and finish in 30 minutes

exercises.prompt: Eucalyptus wood should NOT be used for smoking food because it releases toxic ___ and resins into the smoke.
exercises.explanation: Eucalyptus contains high concentrations of eucalyptol (1,8-cineole) and other monoterpene compounds. When burned, these produce acrid smoke with compounds that are irritants and potentially carcinogenic at the concentrations produced by heavy smoking.

exercises.prompt: A batch of biltong has been hanging for 6 days. The exterior is dark and firm but when you press the thickest strip, the centre still feels slightly soft. What should you do?
exercises.explanation:
Correct. The drying endpoint is firmness throughout — no softness anywhere when pressed. A soft core means moisture and potential microbial activity remain. Extend drying time.

Why the other options are wrong: A soft centre means moisture is still above 20 % in the interior. Mould and potential pathogen growth can occur in the moist core. Continue drying. Commercial biltong ranges from 'wet' (20 % moisture, refrigerate and consume in days) to 'dry' (< 15 % moisture, room-temperature stable). For unrefrigerated storage, you need the dry version. Refrigeration will slow spoilage but doesn't complete the drying process. You need to finish the dehydration, not arrest it.

options.text: It is ready — colour and firmness of the exterior indicate complete drying
The softness is normal — biltong is always slightly moist in the centre
Brush the surface with vinegar and refrigerate immediately to stop spoilage
Continue drying for 1–2 more days; the strips are not yet fully cured

lessons.title: Seed Saving & Storage: The Foundation of Food Sovereignty
lessons.titleSw: Kuhifadhi Mbegu: Msingi wa Uhuru wa Chakula
lessons.briefing: Every food system begins with seed. Saving seed from your best plants — selecting for local adaptation, yield, and flavour — is the original act of agriculture, practiced for 10,000 years before the seed industry existed. This day teaches selection criteria, extraction and drying protocols, viability testing, and long-term storage techniques that protect seed for multiple seasons. A community that controls its seed controls its food.
lessons.briefingSw: Kila mfumo wa chakula huanza na mbegu. Kuhifadhi mbegu kutoka kwa mimea yako bora — kuchagua kwa ajili ya urekebishaji wa ndani, mavuno, na ladha — ni tendo la asili la kilimo, kilichofanywa kwa miaka 10,000 kabla ya sekta ya mbegu kuwepo.
lessons.outline:
1. Why seed saving matters: biodiversity, cost, and food sovereignty
2. Open-pollinated varieties (OPV) vs. hybrids — which seeds you can save
3. Isolation distances and preventing cross-pollination
4. Selection criteria: 10 % rule, performance traits, and negative selection
5. Extraction protocols: wet process (tomato, cucumber) vs. dry process (beans, maize)
6. Drying seed to the target moisture content (≤ 8 % for long storage)
7. Viability testing: germination test and tetrazolium (TZ) test
8. Long-term storage: temperature, humidity, containers, and the Rule of 100

exercises.prompt: A farmer saves seeds from her best-looking H614D maize hybrid plants. Next season she plants 100 % saved seed. What outcome should she expect?
exercises.explanation:
Correct. Hybrid vigour (heterosis) depends on the specific genetic combination of the F₁ cross. F₂ plants are genetically diverse and unpredictable. Save seed only from OPV or landrace varieties.

Why the other options are wrong: H614D is an F₁ hybrid. Saved seed is F₂, which undergoes genetic segregation. The uniform trait combinations that create hybrid vigour break apart. Yield typically drops 20–50 % compared to purchased F₁ seed. Selecting the best-looking plants cannot overcome genetic segregation in hybrids. The loss of heterosis is a genetic consequence, not a management failure. This is the fundamental distinction in seed saving. Hybrids are specifically bred so that only the F₁ generation produces predictable, uniform, high-yielding plants.

options.text: Severe yield loss of 20–50 % due to F₂ genetic segregation — the hybrid vigour is lost
Yields identical to the purchased hybrid — the plants will look the same
Slight yield improvement — the seeds have been selected from the best plants
No difference — hybrid and OPV seeds behave the same when saved

exercises.prompt: The Rule of 100 states that the sum of storage temperature in °F and relative humidity % should not exceed ___ for long-term seed viability.
exercises.explanation: This empirical rule from FAO seed storage research shows that at lower temperatures, higher humidity can be tolerated and vice versa. The key insight: cooling a seed store has the same viability-extending benefit as dehumidifying it.

exercises.prompt:
Practical assessment: Seed viability test setup.

Using at least 25 seeds of any local bean, maize, or cowpea variety:
1. Moisten a paper towel or newspaper until damp (not dripping).
2. Arrange the seeds in a single layer; roll or fold the towel.
3. Place in a labelled plastic bag at room temperature.
4. Photograph your test setup showing:
   a) The labelled bag clearly
   b) The date written on the label
   c) The approximate count of seeds (count written on label or paper)
5. Upload this photo to record your Day 5 practical exercise.

A field officer or peer reviewer will verify your setup and prompt you
to submit a follow-up photo of germination results at Day 7 and Day 14.

rubric.criterion: Seeds arranged in single layer (not stacked)
Paper/towel is moist, not dripping
Label shows date and variety name or description
Minimum 25 seeds visible in photo
Setup is in a sealed or semi-sealed bag to retain moisture

lessons.title: Directional Felling, Chainsaw Physics & Sawlog Grading
lessons.titleSw: Kuangusha Miti kwa Usahihi, Fizikia ya Msumeno wa Moto na Upimaji Magogo
lessons.briefing: Felling a 20-ton hardwood tree is one of the most hazardous operations in field engineering; an uncontrolled fall will crush workers, smash equipment, shatter valuable sawlogs, or trigger deadly 'barber-chair' trunk splits. True forestry is not about hacking at a stump; it is the precision science of internal hinge engineering—using an open-face directional notch, a calculated holding wood hinge (10% of trunk diameter), wedges, and an established 45-degree retreat path. This lesson covers chainsaw kickback zone physics, chainsaw chain sharpening geometry, directional felling mechanics, and sawlog scaling/grading formulas.
lessons.outline: Personal protective equipment (PPE: ballistic kevlar chaps, steel-toe boots, mesh visor helmet, hearing protection); chainsaw anatomy and safety features (inertia chain brake, chain catcher, throttle interlock); kickback physics: the upper quadrant of the guide bar tip (rotational energy vector); chain filing geometry (30° cutter top-plate angle, 0.025-inch depth gauge / raker height); assessing tree hazards (dead snags, rot, lean, crown weight distribution, wind speed); directional felling cuts: the Open-Face notch (70° opening, depth 20-25% diameter), the Bore Cut (plunge cut) to prevent barber-chairing on heavy leaning trees, and the Back Cut; holding wood hinge thickness rule (10% of DBH); felling wedges; establishing the 45° escape retreat route; sawlog grading and volume calculation (Huber's and Smalian's cubic volume formulas).

exercises.prompt: A certified logger is preparing to fell a 50 cm diameter cypress tree using an open-face notch. What is the required thickness of the uncut holding wood hinge, and what is its mechanical function during the fall?
exercises.explanation:
The universal forestry rule: Hinge thickness = 10% of DBH (50 cm × 0.10 = 5 cm). The hinge wood holds the falling trunk in tension and compression, preventing the tree from rolling off course into power lines or workers.

Why the other options are wrong: A 15 cm hinge is too thick; the tree will hang up or tear wood fibers, refusing to fall. A 0.5 cm hinge snaps instantly, losing all directional control. Cutting through completely produces an uncontrolled free-falling tree that can crush the sawyer.

options.text: 15 cm thick (30% of trunk diameter)
0.5 cm thick (1% of trunk diameter)
5 cm thick (10% of trunk diameter); the hinge acts as an internal wooden pivot that guides the tree along the planned path while preventing lateral twisting or premature backward kickoff
Cut completely through with zero hinge

exercises.prompt: On a chainsaw guide bar, the upper 90-degree quadrant of the tip is designated as the ___ zone, where chain contact throws the running saw violently upward toward the operator's face in less than ___ milliseconds.
exercises.explanation: The upper tip quadrant is the kickback zone. Impact here generates violent rotational energy that hurls the saw upward before human reflexes can respond.

exercises.prompt: Match each directional felling component to its geometric specification.
exercises.explanation: Notch aims the fall; stump step blocks kick-off; bore cuts prevent barber-chairs; 45° paths save lives.

right.text: 50° to 70° wide opening cut facing target landing zone (20-25% tree depth)
Placing the back cut 2.5 to 5.0 cm higher than the notch apex to block kickback
Plunging bar through trunk to establish hinge before severing rear trigger strap
Cleared retreat route walking diagonally backward away from the falling canopy

exercises.prompt: Why is the 'Bore Cut' (plunging the chainsaw bar through the trunk behind the hinge) strictly required when felling trees with a severe forward lean?
exercises.explanation:
In leaning trees, tension in rear fibers is massive. Starting from the outside back causes the trunk to split vertically upwards (barber-chair), killing the logger. The bore cut builds the hinge safely from the inside, leaving a rear strap of wood that is severed last.

Why the other options are wrong: Bore cutting consumes more power and fuel; its sole purpose is survival and safety. Leaning trees are usually solid wood; the issue is severe mechanical tension. Bore cuts test chain sharpness, but the technique is for fracture prevention.

options.text: To save two-stroke fuel during felling

Heavy forward-leaning trees carry extreme tension in their rear wood fibers; a standard rear cut triggers a violent 'barber-chair' vertical trunk explosion, whereas a bore cut leaves a rear strap that holds the tree safely until released
Because leaning trees are always hollow in the center
To make the chain teeth dull evenly on both sides

exercises.prompt: Using Smalian's cubic volume formula V = [π × (Ds² + Dl²) / 8] × L, a 5.0-metre sawlog with small-end diameter of 0.40 m and large-end diameter of 0.60 m has a solid log volume of approximately ___ cubic metres.

lessons.title: Timber Conversion — Pit Sawing & Chainsaw Mills
lessons.titleSw: Upasuaji Magogo — Misumeno ya Mashimo (Pit Sawing) na Mashine za Msumeno
lessons.briefing: A round tree trunk lying in the mud cannot frame a clinic or build a bridge; it must be converted into dimensioned structural lumber (posts, rafters, purlins, planks). In remote forests without heavy industrial band sawmills, lumber conversion relies on two decentralized technologies: the classical two-man Pit Saw (zero-fuel manual conversion using human muscle) and the portable Chainsaw Alaskan Mill (gasoline-powered precision slabbing). This lesson covers log debarking, chalk line layout geometry, saw tooth set and kerf thickness calculations, pit sawyer roles (Topman vs Pitman), ripping chain geometry (10° top plate angle), and sawing patterns (through-and-through vs quarter sawing).
lessons.outline: Log preparation: debarking to eliminate grit/stones, end-coating with wax to prevent drying checks; snapping parallel layout chalk lines; the mechanics of the Two-Man Pit Saw (long tapered blade, 2.0 to 2.5 m, rip-filed teeth cutting on the downstroke); crew roles: the Topman (steers line from above) and the Pitman (powers downstroke in the pit); portable Chainsaw Alaskan Mills: aluminum guide rails, clamp carriages; the physics of the Ripping Chain (10° cutter angle vs standard 30° crosscut, scoring wood along end grain); kerf width analysis (3 mm pit saw vs 9 mm chainsaw mill) and percentage recovery yields; sawing patterns: Plain/Through-and-Through vs Quarter Sawing.

exercises.prompt: A sawyer is setting up a 70cc chainsaw with an Alaskan mill to rip a hardwood log into dimensional framing planks. Why must a specialized 'Ripping Chain' with a 10° cutter top-plate angle be installed instead of a standard 30° crosscut chain?
exercises.explanation:
Cutting parallel to wood grain requires a planing chisel action (10° angle). Standard 30° crosscut teeth tear long strings that wrap around the clutch drum and pack the bar gullet, causing severe engine bogging and rough, grooved boards.

Why the other options are wrong: There is no legal restriction; it is a purely mechanical wood-cutting physics problem. Engine RPM is limited by the governor; ripping chains actually experience higher resistance. Ripping chains must be filed frequently due to high end-grain wear.

options.text: The 10° cutter angle acts like a miniature plane, shaving end-grain fibers cleanly into fine chips, whereas 30° crosscut teeth tear out long stringy 'angel-hair' fibers that instantly choke the saw sprocket and stall the engine
Because 30° chains are illegal to use on fallen logs
To make the chainsaw run twice as fast
Because 10° chains never need sharpening

exercises.prompt: In traditional two-man pit sawing, the saw blade is designed to cut wood strictly on the ___ stroke, driven by the body weight of the ___ standing beneath the log inside the pit.
exercises.explanation: The teeth point downward with negative rake; cutting occurs on the downstroke powered by the Pitman below, while the Topman above steers the line and lifts.

exercises.prompt: Match each primary log conversion concept to its technical definition.
exercises.explanation: Spudding cleans logs; end-sealing stops cracks; kerf is cutting waste; quarter-sawing creates dimensionally stable non-cupping planks.

right.text: Peeling outer bark to eliminate embedded grit that dulls saw teeth
Slows longitudinal water evaporation to prevent destructive radial end-checking
The width of wood pulverized into sawdust by the thickness of the cutting blade
Boards with growth rings at 60°-90° providing maximum resistance to cupping

exercises.prompt: A community has harvested 5 valuable timber logs and needs to produce 25 mm thick roofing boards. Why might the community choose manual pit sawing over an Alaskan chainsaw mill for this specific job?
exercises.explanation:
Kerf thickness is critical when cutting thin 25 mm boards. A chainsaw blade grinds 10 mm into dust for every 25 mm board cut (destroying nearly a third of the tree). The thin 3 mm pit saw blade produces 20-25% more finished boards from scarce timber.

Why the other options are wrong: Pit sawing is exhausting, grueling manual labor. Chainsaws cut hardwoods easily, but waste significant wood volume as kerf. All green lumber must be dried before construction regardless of conversion method.

options.text: The pit saw's narrow 3 mm kerf recovers nearly 90% of the log volume as usable boards, whereas the chainsaw mill's 10 mm kerf turns nearly 30% of the log into wasted sawdust
Because pit sawing requires zero human physical effort
Because chainsaws cannot cut hardwood trees
Because pit-sawn lumber does not require drying

exercises.prompt: Alternate teeth on a pit saw blade are bent slightly to the left and right in a mechanical adjustment called the ___, which creates a kerf wider than the blade body to prevent the saw from ___ inside the cut.
exercises.explanation: Tooth set (0.5 mm offset on each side) creates clearance. Without set, wood friction clamps onto the saw blade body, locking it motionless.

lessons.title: Wood Anatomy, Moisture Physics & Solar Kiln Seasoning
lessons.titleSw: Anatomia ya Mbao, Fizikia ya Unyevu na Kukausha kwa Tanuri ya Jua
lessons.briefing: Building a house or bridge with freshly milled 'green' lumber guarantees disaster: as the wood dries, doors jam, wall joints pull apart, trusses twist into corkscrews, and severe fungal rot sets in. Freshly cut wood contains up to 100% moisture by dry weight. Timber does not shrink uniformly; it shrinks twice as much tangentially along growth rings as it does radially, creating massive internal drying stresses. This lesson covers wood cell anatomy, Free Water vs Bound Water, the Fiber Saturation Point (FSP at ~28%), calculating Moisture Content (MC%), stacking protocols with stickers, and building a low-cost passive greenhouse Solar Lumber Kiln that seasons timber to 12% MC in 3 weeks.
lessons.outline: Wood microstructure: Heartwood (dead, durable, dense) vs Sapwood (living, sap-filled, vulnerable to beetles); microscopic tracheids and vessels; the physics of wood moisture: Free Water (inside cell cavities) vs Bound Water (adsorbed chemically in cell walls); the Fiber Saturation Point (FSP = 28% to 30% MC) where shrinkage begins; Moisture Content formula: MC% = [(Wet Weight - Dry Weight) / Dry Weight] * 100; differential shrinkage ratio (Tangential 8% vs Radial 4% vs Longitudinal 0.1%); air drying stacking architecture (level foundation, 25 mm square stickers aligned vertically, overhang roofs, weighted stacks); greenhouse solar kiln construction (semi-transparent corrugated poly roof, black heat-absorber baffle wall, solar-powered 12V circulation fans).

exercises.prompt: A woodworker mills green eucalyptus lumber at 80% moisture content. As the wood dries down from 80% to 30%, what happens to the physical dimensions of the boards?
exercises.explanation:
Between initial green moisture (>80%) and the Fiber Saturation Point (approx. 28-30%), water leaves only the open lumens. Dimensional shrinkage begins strictly when 'bound water' starts leaving the cell walls below 28% MC.

Why the other options are wrong: Shrinkage does not occur above the Fiber Saturation Point. Drying never causes swelling; water loss causes weight loss and subsequent shrinkage. Honeycombing occurs during rapid high-heat drying below FSP, not during initial free-water loss.

options.text: The boards shrink by half their width
The boards swell and become thicker
The boards lose physical weight but experience virtually zero dimensional shrinkage, because only 'free water' in the hollow cell cavities is evaporating, while cell walls remain fully saturated
The boards develop severe internal honeycomb cracks

exercises.prompt: The critical threshold in timber seasoning where all free water has left the cell cavities but the cell walls remain fully saturated with bound water—occurring at approximately 28% to 30% moisture content—is called the Fiber ___ Point.
exercises.explanation: The Fiber Saturation Point (FSP, ~28% MC) is the exact physical boundary where all wood shrinkage and strength gains begin.

exercises.prompt: Match each timber moisture concept to its scientific definition.
exercises.explanation: Heartwood is durable; sapwood is bug-prone; bound water causes shrinkage; tangential shrinkage causes boards to cup.

right.text: Dense, chemically plugged central tree core naturally resistant to rot
Outer living ring of water-conducting wood highly vulnerable to beetles
Moisture chemically adsorbed within cell walls whose loss triggers shrinkage
Shrinkage along growth rings (approx. twice radial shrinkage) causing cupping

exercises.prompt: When stacking green timber for air seasoning, why must the thin wooden spacer strips ('stickers') be placed in dead vertical alignment directly above each other?
exercises.explanation:
Wet wood is plastic and deforms easily under load. If stickers are staggered, downward weight bends the planks between supports. Once dry, the wavy bends set permanently into the wood, ruining structural flatness.

Why the other options are wrong: Climbing lumber stacks is a safety violation; stickers are purely for airflow and support. Stickers provide no termite barrier; foundation elevation achieves that. Stickers actually risk leaving 'sticker stain' marks if wet; alignment is purely for mechanical straightness.

options.text: To make the stack easier to climb
To keep termites from walking across the boards
Misaligned stickers cause the immense weight of the stacked lumber to act as an un-supported bending load on the wet boards, permanently bending and warping the timber into wavy sags as it dries
To change the color of the lumber

exercises.prompt: A small test block of green timber weighs 360 grams. After baking in an oven at 103°C until all moisture is driven out, its constant dry weight is 200 grams. The moisture content (MC %) of the timber was ___ percent.

lessons.title: Timber Preservation — Borates, Pyroligneous Tar & Termite Defense
lessons.titleSw: Kuhifadhi Mbao — Dawa ya Borate, Lami ya Asili na Kuzuia Mchwa
lessons.briefing: In tropical East Africa, untreated softwood or sapwood timber installed in the ground is hollowed out by subterranean termites (*Macrotermes*) and powder-post beetles within 12 to 24 months. Industrial chromated copper arsenate (CCA) pressure treatment is toxic and unavailable off-grid. A self-reliant community must deploy sustainable wood preservation: diffusion borate salts (disodium octaborate tetrahydrate), hot wood-pyrolysis creosote/tar coatings, char-and-soak ground post hardening, the Boucherie sap-displacement method for green poles, and physical galvanized metal 'termite shields' on foundation masonry.
lessons.outline: The biological enemies of timber: Subterranean Termites (Macrotermes, workers building shelter mud tubes), Powder-Post Beetles (Lyctus, Bostrichidae infesting high-starch sapwood), and Brown Rot / White Rot fungi; chemical preservation classes: Water-Borne Borates (DOT: Disodium Octaborate Tetrahydrate) for interior framing, and Oil-Borne Preservatives (refined wood tar creosote from Day 5 pyrolysis + motor oil) for ground contact; the Boucherie Sap Displacement method (gravity tank displacing sap in green poles with copper sulfate/borate); hot-and-cold bath thermal soaking; the Char-and-Tar fence post protocol; mechanical termite shields (ant caps: 26-gauge galvanized steel turned down at 45°); building design biosecurity (200 mm clearance above grade).

exercises.prompt: A builder uses a 10% disodium octaborate tetrahydrate (borate) solution to treat timber. Why can borate-treated lumber be used for interior roof trusses and wall studs, but is strictly prohibited for outdoor ground-contact fence posts?
exercises.explanation:
Borates are fantastic, non-toxic, deep-penetrating insecticides, but they are fully leachable. Under roof cover, borates last for centuries. Outdoors in ground contact, rain leaches the boron away, allowing termites and fungi to destroy the wood.

Why the other options are wrong: Borates are non-metallic mineral salts; they have no lightning attraction. Borates are chemically stable under UV radiation. Borate solutions dry completely clear and colorless.

options.text: Borates attract lightning strikes outdoors
Outdoor sunlight turns borate into acid that dissolves wood
Borate turns timber black which looks unattractive

Borate salts remain water-soluble and do not chemically fix to wood fibers; outdoor rainfall and ground moisture will leach the preservative out into the soil within months, leaving the post completely unprotected against subterranean termites

exercises.prompt: In the Boucherie sap-displacement method for treating green eucalyptus poles, preservative liquid is fed from an elevated reservoir under ___ pressure into one end of the fresh log, pushing the natural tree ___ out the opposite end.
exercises.explanation: Gravity head pressure (0.5 to 1.0 bar from a 5-10 m high tank) pushes chemical solution straight through the living open sapwood vessels, displacing the sap.

exercises.prompt: Match each timber preservation method to its operational mechanism.
exercises.explanation: Termite shields block tubes; char-and-tar protects posts; borates protect indoor wood; clearance prevents ground rot.

right.text: 45° downward metal lip blocking subterranean termite shelter mud tubes
Creates a 3mm carbonized non-edible layer soaked in hot antiseptic wood pitch
Water-borne metabolic stomach poison for termites in interior framing
Elevating timber framing on concrete piers to prevent ground moisture wicking

exercises.prompt: A homeowner inspects a wooden building and finds piles of fine, flour-like wood powder (frass) beneath the structural beams, accompanied by tiny 1 mm round pinholes in the wood. What pest has infested the timber?
exercises.explanation:
Powder-post beetles attack high-starch sapwood. The larvae bore invisible tunnels for months, packing them with fine flour-like frass, and adults chew round 1 mm pinholes when emerging.

Why the other options are wrong: Termites construct mud tubes and leave hollow cavities filled with brown soil, not dry flour powder and clean pinholes. Woodpeckers leave large jagged ragged holes, not 1 mm pinholes. Carpenter ants kick out coarse wood shavings like pencil sharpenings, not fine flour-like frass.

options.text: Subterranean termites
Powder-post beetles (Lyctus / Bostrichidae), whose internal larvae feed on starch in the sapwood, turning the interior into powder and leaving exit pinholes
Woodpeckers
Carpenter ants

exercises.prompt: Wood-decay fungi (brown rot and white rot) cannot survive or digest timber if the wood's moisture content is maintained below ___ percent, reinforcing the importance of proper roof overhangs and sub-floor ventilation.
exercises.explanation: Wood-destroying fungi require liquid water in the cell walls; dry wood below 20% MC is biologically immune to fungal decay.

lessons.title: Heavy Timber Joinery & Structural Truss Framing
lessons.titleSw: Viungio vya Mbao Nzito na Uundaji wa Paa za Truss
lessons.briefing: Steel gusset plates and threaded bolts are convenient, but in isolated wilderness installations where metal hardware is unavailable, buildings must stand on the timeless engineering of Heavy Timber Joinery. For thousands of years, monumental cathedrals, covered bridges, and Japanese temples stood without a single metallic nail, held together by interlocking mortise-and-tenon joints, draw-bored hardwood pegs, and timber scarf splices. This capstone lesson covers structural stress vectors (tension, compression, shear), classic joinery geometry, layout using the Square Rule, draw-boring physics, King Post roof truss engineering, and field inspection rubrics.
lessons.outline: Structural forces in timber frames: tension (pulling apart), compression (pushing together), and horizontal shear parallel to grain; the classic Mortise-and-Tenon joint (1/3 thickness rule, cheek layout, shoulder cutting); Draw-Boring mechanics (offset peg hole by 2-3 mm, tapered dry oak/acacia peg pulling the joint permanently tight under tension); the Scarf Joint (halved and bladed scarf with key) for splicing short logs into 12-metre ridge beams; the King Post Roof Truss (tie beam, principal rafters, king post in tension, compressive struts); birdsmouth rafter seat cuts; PHOTO_CAPTURE assessment rubric of timber joinery, truss framing, or solar kiln.

exercises.prompt: In traditional heavy timber framing, what is the mechanical purpose of 'Draw-Boring' a mortise-and-tenon joint with an offset peg hole?
exercises.explanation:
Draw-boring eliminates the need for clamps or glue. The 2.5 mm offset creates a mechanical wedging action as the peg is driven, sucking the joint faces together into an indestructible, airtight structural connection that self-tightens under load.

Why the other options are wrong: Draw-bored pegs are locked permanently under tension; they cannot be removed by hand. Auger bits drill through assembled wood easily, but straight holes provide zero pulling tension. The purpose of draw-boring is rigid structural lockup, not sliding.

options.text: To make the peg easier to remove with fingers
Because drilling straight through assembled wood splits the auger bit
To allow the joint to slide back and forth in earthquakes

Boring the hole through the tenon 2.5 mm closer to the shoulder forces the tapered hardwood peg to act as a powerful mechanical cam, pulling the tenon shoulders permanently tight against the mortise face with thousands of pounds of tension

exercises.prompt: According to the universal rule of heavy timber mortise-and-tenon joinery, the thickness of the central tenon tongue should be exactly ___ of the total timber beam thickness.
exercises.explanation: The 1/3 rule balances strength equally between the tenon tongue in bending and the two female mortise cheeks in shear.

exercises.prompt: Match each heavy timber truss component to its primary structural stress.
exercises.explanation: Rafters are compressed; tie beams are pulled in tension; the King Post hangs in tension; struts push in compression.

right.text: Heavy axial compression transferring roof gravity and wind loads down
Pure horizontal tension preventing the rafters from spreading the walls apart
Pure vertical tension; hangs from apex to pull the tie beam upward against sagging
Compression props supporting the mid-span of principal rafters against deflection

exercises.prompt: Why are large heavy timber framing members (e.g. 200 mm × 200 mm posts and beams) considered to possess superior fire resistance compared to unprotected light structural steel?
exercises.explanation:
Unprotected steel beams lose 50% of structural yield strength at 500°C and collapse catastrophically within 15 minutes of a building fire. Massive heavy timber chars at 0.6 mm per minute; the insulating char blocks heat, preserving a solid load-bearing core for hours.

Why the other options are wrong: Wood is combustible, but massive cross-sections char slowly and predictably. Wood releases combustible pyroligneous gases, not inert nitrogen. Timber framing is solid wood, not filled with concrete.

options.text: Heavy timbers burn slowly from the outside inward, forming a dense insulating charcoal crust (0.6 mm/min) that shields the interior load-bearing core, while structural steel rapidly softens and buckles at 500°C
Because heavy timber cannot catch fire under any circumstances
Because wood releases nitrogen gas when heated
Because timber frames are filled with concrete

exercises.prompt: Photograph a heavy timber mortise-and-tenon joint, roof truss assembly, pit-sawing setup, chainsaw milling rig, or solar lumber seasoning stack from your forestry and timber engineering field practice. Ensure the image clearly displays structural joinery, peg fastening, wood grain orientation, or drying sticker alignment, and include your written dimensional inspection report.
exercises.explanation: Photographic documentation of timber joinery, wood seasoning stacks, or milling rigs verifies practical craftsmanship and engineering compliance with structural load-bearing and wood preservation standards.

rubric.criterion: Photograph clearly shows mortise-and-tenon joint, timber truss, milling rig, or stickered drying stack
Carpentry details (square shoulders, draw-bore pegs, scarf joints) or forestry setups are distinctly visible
Written report records timber species, moisture content estimate, joint dimensions, and design load role
Image is well-lit, in sharp focus, showing clean woodworking tolerances and safe workshop practices

lessons.title: Colour, relaxer, and chemical safety
lessons.titleSw: Rangi, relaxer, na kemikali
lessons.briefing:
Patch-test colour and some relaxers as the manufacturer and college require. Mix ratios (developer volumes) are chemistry. 40 volume is not a shortcut for 20 volume on a scalp. Timing starts when application is complete; over-processing burns.

PPE: gloves, and apron. Bleach dust is not for inhaling. Do not mix products you cannot name. Never use metallic dye then oxidise without knowing the reaction risk.

Strand tests tell you if the hair will survive. Overlapping relaxer on previously relaxed hair is a classic breakage. Apply to new growth as specified.

Emergency: product in eyes — rinse and seek help. Keep SDS. Neutralise relaxer as directed; water alone is not always the full story.
lessons.briefingSw: Fanya patch test. Fuata ratio ya developer. Usiweke 40 volume kichwani ovyo. PPE. Usichanganye bidhaa usizozifahamu. Strand test. Overlap ya relaxer inavunja nywele.

exercises.prompt: Why is a patch test used before some colour services?
exercises.explanation: Follow product timing. Document the result.

options.text: To bill extra time
To check for allergic reaction before full-scalp application
To bleach the floor
NITA requires it for water only

exercises.prompt: Overlapping relaxer onto already relaxed lengths often causes:
exercises.explanation: Apply to new growth. Protect lengths.

options.text: Extra shine only
Breakage
Permanent patch tests
Lower pH automatically

exercises.prompt: Developer volume (10, 20, 30, 40) is mainly about:
exercises.explanation: Wrong volume is a chemical burn risk.

options.text: Bottle size
Lift / oxidising strength — using too high on scalp burns
Water temperature
Comb colour

exercises.prompt: If colour enters the eye you should:
exercises.explanation: Stop the service. Irrigate. Record.

options.text: Rub with a towel of bleach
Rinse with water and get medical help as SOP
Apply more colour to equalise
Ignore it

exercises.prompt: A test on a small section of hair to see the result before full application is a ___ test.
exercises.explanation: Strand tests check breakage and colour result.

exercises.prompt: Hair snaps when you comb during relaxer processing. Trainee wants to leave it on “so it finishes”. You:
exercises.explanation: Breakage during processing is a stop condition.

options.text: Leave it — breakage means it is working
Rinse/neutralise immediately per manufacturer and treat as an emergency over-process
Add more lye
Blow-dry on high to strengthen

lessons.title: Cutting finish, styling heat, and aftercare
lessons.titleSw: Kumalizia kukata, heat, na aftercare
lessons.briefing:
A haircut is checked in the mirror and with the head in movement, not only on a still mannequin. Balance both sides. Cross-check. Do not hide a mistake with excessive thinning that will spike in two weeks.

Heat tools: temperature suitable for the hair’s condition. Heat protectant is not optional on already chemical-processed hair. Burns on ears and necks are professionalism failures.

Aftercare: which shampoo, how soon to wash colour, how to sleep on a silk scarf if that is the method, and when to return. Selling a product is fine; lying about what the chemical did is not.

Clean the station before the next client. Hair on the floor is a slip and a hygiene fail.
lessons.briefingSw: Kagua cut pande zote. Heat protectant kwenye nywele ya kemikali. Usiwasha masikio. Eleza aftercare. Safisha kituo kabla ya mteja mwingine.

exercises.prompt: Cross-checking a haircut means:

Patch test
Type of bond

exercises.prompt: Client hates the length after you cut. They asked for “a trim”. You cut 8 cm. Professional response?

lessons.title: Hygiene, consultation, and professional conduct
lessons.titleSw: Usafi, ushauri, na maadili
lessons.briefing:
Salon work is a health trade. Wash hands, sanitise or sterilise tools to the salon SOP, and change towels. Blood on a blade goes in a sharps container, not the general bin. Do not work with open wounds on your hands without covering as policy says.

Consultation is assessment: scalp, history of relaxer/colour, allergies, and what the client actually wants. Photographs help. If the scalp is broken, you do not apply relaxer “gently”. Refuse, explain, reschedule or refer.

Records protect the client and the college: products, batch if required, and patch-test outcome. Gossip about a scalp condition is unprofessional.

Gowning and posture prevent product on clothes and injury to you during long cutting sessions.

lessons.title: Food hygiene and temperature control
lessons.titleSw: Usafi wa chakula na joto
lessons.briefing:
The danger zone for bacterial growth is approximately 5–60 °C. Keep cold food cold and hot food hot. Do not leave cooked stew on the pass overnight “to cool slowly in a deep pot”. Cool quickly in shallow containers as taught, then refrigerate.

Separate raw and cooked: boards, knives, cloths. Colour-coded boards exist because chicken juice on a salad is an outbreak. Wash hands after raw protein, after the toilet, and after handling refuse.

FIFO stock rotation. Date labels. A dented blown can is not a bargain. Report pest signs; do not hide droppings with a mat.

Personal hygiene: hair restrained, wounds covered with a waterproof dressing, no jewellery that falls in food. That is the unit, not extra politeness.
lessons.briefingSw: Danger zone takriban 5–60 °C. Tenganisha mbichi na iliyopikwa. Poza haraka. FIFO. Funga vidonda. Funga nywele.

lessons.title: Knives, fire, and kitchen hazards
lessons.titleSw: Visu, moto, na hatari jikoni
lessons.briefing:
A chip-pan / fat fire is fought by turning off heat if safe, covering with a lid, and using the correct extinguisher. Never water — it explodes the oil into a fireball. Know the extinguisher types in your kitchen.

Knives: carry point down, pass handle first, cut on a stable board with fingers tucked. A falling knife is not caught. Sharp knives are safer than dull ones because they do not slip.

Floors: clean spills immediately. “I’ll mop at close” is how ankles break mid-service. Lids on pots, handles inward, and dry cloths on hot handles.

First aid box and burns protocol. Oil burns are serious. Cool with running water as trained, then report.
lessons.briefingSw: Usitumie maji kwenye moto wa mafuta. Funika na zima moto. Chukua kisu ncha chini. Futa mafuriko mara moja. Visu vikali ni salama kuliko butu.

lessons.title: Service, mise en place, and complaints
lessons.titleSw: Huduma, mise en place, na malalamiko
lessons.briefing:
Mise en place means everything in its place before service: garnishes cut, stations stocked, glasses polished. Panic during service is usually poor prep, not fate.

Greet, inform, and serve from the correct side as the style requires. Hot plates are warned. Dietary needs are not a joke — allergen contamination can hospitalise.

Complaints: listen, apologise without arguing, replace or remove, tell the supervisor, log. A hair in soup is not a debate about protein. The guest is not always right about the recipe, but they are always heard.

Close-down is hygiene: labelling, temperatures, and a clean pass so the morning brigade does not inherit your mess.
lessons.briefingSw: Mise en place kabla ya service. Allergens ni hatari. Malalamiko: sikiliza, samahani, badilisha, log. Usibishane kuhusu nywele kwenye supu.

lessons.title: Mortar, bond, and the first course
lessons.titleSw: Chokaa, bond, na kozi ya kwanza
lessons.briefing:
A wall is only as true as the first course. Level and line it until you are bored of checking. Any error is multiplied as you rise. Butter heads for full perpends; empty perpends leak and fail compressive paths.

Mortar: follow the job spec (a common teaching mix for general blockwork is in the region of 1:4 cement:sand — never invent a wetter mix to make laying “easy”). Too much water weakens and stains. Mix small enough to use before it dies. Do not retemper with extra water hours later if the spec forbids it.

Bond (stretcher, English, etc.) must run correctly so vertical joints do not align one above the other except where the bond requires. Quoins are your plumbing posts — get them up with a level and line pins.

Joint thickness consistent. Fat joints on one course and hairline on the next is a fail even if the wall stands.
lessons.briefingSw: Kozi ya kwanza ni msingi. Level na line. Fuata mchanganyiko wa chokaa. Perpends zijazwe. Bond isizuie joints kuwa wima moja juu ya nyingine isipokuwa bond inavyosema.

exercises.explanation: A lean first course cannot be fixed higher without a visible correction.

exercises.explanation: Full mortar beds and perpends as specified.

options.text: Faster curing always

Automatic square

options.text: Improves spec strength
Weakens the mix
Squares the quoin
Replaces lime

exercises.explanation: Bond pattern is structural and visual.

options.text: Perfect work
Broken bond / setting-out error
Stronger perpends
A type of damp-proof course

exercises.prompt: The vertical mortar joint between block ends is a ___.
exercises.explanation: Perpends should be full and aligned to the bond.

exercises.explanation: Catching up makes tapering joints and a drunk wall.

lessons.title: Plumb, line, curing, and weather
lessons.titleSw: Plumb, line, curing, na hali ya hewa
lessons.briefing:
Check plumb and line every few courses, not only at the end of the day. Corner profiles and a line keep the face true. Raking back or toothing as specified if you stop a length.

Green mortar fears sun and rain. Cure: keep it damp as taught; do not let it bake on day one. Incoming rain: cover the wall; do not add extra storeys onto weak beds. Washout of cement from joints is a defect.

Joint finishing (flush, tooled) is done at the right stiffness — too early and you smear; too late and you polish a cracked skin. Brush excess without staining the face.

Leave weep holes and DPCs as the drawing shows. A beautiful wall that bridges the DPC with mortar droppings can still damp.
lessons.briefingSw: Kagua plumb kila baadhi ya kozi. Linda chokaa mpya na mvua na jua. Finish joints kwa wakati. Usiingize mortar kwenye DPC.

exercises.prompt: Rain is coming and today’s mortar is still green on a 1.2 m wall. Right action:
exercises.explanation: Rain washes cement from fresh joints.

options.text: Cover the work and do not load extra height onto weak mortar
Spray diesel
Build two more metres to weight it down
Remove all profiles
